title.zh: 卷53 李孝伯 李衝
title.raw: 卷53 李孝伯 李衝 Volume 53: Li Xiaobo, Li Chong

sentences.zh: 李孝伯 李沖

translations.literal: Li Xiaobo; Li Chong
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiaobo; Li Chong

sentences.zh: 李孝伯，趙郡人也，高平公順從父弟。

translations.literal: Li Xiaobo was a native of Zhao Commandery, a paternal cousin of Duke of Gaoping Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiaobo came from Zhao Commandery and was a paternal cousin of Duke Shun of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 父曾，少治鄭氏禮、左氏春秋，以教授為業。

translations.literal: His father Zeng in his youth studied Zheng's Rites and Zuo's Spring and Autumn Annals, and made his living by teaching.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zeng had studied Zheng's Rites and the Zuo Tradition of the Spring and Autumn Annals in his youth and earned his living as a teacher.

sentences.zh: 郡三辟功曹不就，門人勸之，曾曰：「功曹之職，雖曰鄉選高第，猶是郡吏耳。

translations.literal: The commandery thrice summoned him to serve as Assistant Officer but he did not accept; his disciples urged him, and Zeng said: "The post of Assistant Officer, though called the highest selection of the district, is still merely a commandery clerk.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery summoned him three times to serve as Assistant Officer, but he refused. When his disciples urged him to accept, Zeng said, "The post of Assistant Officer may be called the top choice of the district, but it is still only a commandery clerk.

sentences.zh: 北面事人，亦何容易。

translations.literal: To face north and serve another — how could that be easy?
translations.idiomatic: To face north and serve another person — how could that be easy?

sentences.zh: 」州辟主簿，到官月餘，乃歎曰：「梁叔敬有云：州郡之職，徒勞人耳。

translations.literal: The province summoned him as Registrar; after a month in office he sighed and said: "Liang Shujing once said: posts in provinces and commanderies only wear people out for nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The province then summoned him as Registrar, but after little more than a month in office he sighed and said, "Liang Shujing once remarked that provincial and commandery posts do nothing but exhaust a man.

sentences.zh: 道之不行，身之憂也。

translations.literal: When the Way does not prevail, that is one's own worry."
translations.idiomatic: When the Way does not prevail, that is one's own concern."

sentences.zh: 」遂還家講授。

translations.literal: He then returned home to lecture and teach.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned home to lecture and teach.

sentences.zh: 太祖時，徵拜博士，出為趙郡太守，令行禁止，劫盜奔竄。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Daizu, he was summoned and appointed Erudite, then sent out as Administrator of Zhao Commandery; his orders were enforced and forbidden things halted, and bandits and robbers fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Daizu, he was summoned and appointed Erudite, then sent out as Administrator of Zhao Commandery. His orders were enforced without exception, and bandits and robbers fled the region.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 并州丁零，數為山東之害，知曾能得百姓死力，憚不入境。

translations.literal: The Dingling of Bing Province had repeatedly been a scourge to Shandong; knowing that Zeng could win the people's utmost loyalty, they feared him and did not enter his territory.
translations.idiomatic: The Dingling tribes of Bing Province had long been a menace to Shandong, but knowing that Zeng could command the people's utmost loyalty, they feared to enter his territory.

sentences.zh: 賊於常山界得一死鹿，謂趙郡地也，賊長責之，還令送鹿故處。

translations.literal: Bandits found a dead deer in the Changshan border region and, taking it for Zhao Commandery territory, their chief reprimanded them and had the deer returned to where it had been.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits found a dead deer in the Changshan borderlands and mistook the spot for Zhao Commandery, their chief rebuked them and ordered the deer returned to where it had been found.

sentences.zh: 隣郡為之謠曰：「詐作趙郡鹿，猶勝常山粟。

translations.literal: A neighboring commandery made up a ballad about it: "Feigning a Zhao Commandery deer is still better than Changshan grain."
translations.idiomatic: A neighboring commandery composed a ballad about it: "A fake Zhao Commandery deer is still better than Changshan grain."

sentences.zh: 」其見憚如此。

translations.literal: Such was the fear he inspired.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the fear he inspired.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈平南將軍、荊州刺史、栢仁子，諡曰懿。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously given the titles General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Jing Province, with the noble rank of Baron of Bairen; his posthumous name was Yi.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously appointed General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Jing Province, ennobled as Baron of Bairen, and given the posthumous name Yi.

sentences.zh: 孝伯少傳父業，博綜羣言。

translations.literal: Xiaobo in his youth inherited his father's learning and mastered many fields of discourse.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Xiaobo inherited his father's learning and mastered a wide range of texts.

sentences.zh: 美風儀，動有法度。

translations.literal: He had a handsome bearing and deportment, and his every movement conformed to propriety.
translations.idiomatic: He had a handsome bearing, and his every movement conformed to propriety.

sentences.zh: 從兄順言之於世祖，徵為中散，世祖見而異之，謂順曰：「真卿家千里駒也。

translations.literal: His older cousin Shun spoke of him to Emperor Shizu; he was summoned as Palatial Attendant. The emperor, upon meeting him, remarked on his distinction and said to Shun: "Truly a thousand-li colt of your house."
translations.idiomatic: His older cousin Shun recommended him to Emperor Shizu, and he was summoned to serve as Palatial Attendant. When the emperor met him, he was struck by his quality and said to Shun, "Truly a thousand-li colt of your house."

sentences.zh: 」遷祕書奏事中散，轉侍郎、光祿大夫，賜爵南昌子，加建威將軍，委以軍國機密，甚見親寵。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Palatial Attendant for Memorials in the Secretariat, then transferred to Gentleman and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness; he was granted the noble rank of Baron of Nanchang and given the additional title General Who Establishes Might; he was entrusted with military and state secrets and was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palatial Attendant for Memorials in the Secretariat, then transferred to Gentleman and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness. He was ennobled as Baron of Nanchang, given the additional title General Who Establishes Might, entrusted with military and state secrets, and greatly favored.

sentences.zh: 謀謨切祕，時人莫能知也。

translations.literal: His counsels and plans were utterly confidential; people of the time could not know them.
translations.idiomatic: His counsels and plans were kept utterly secret, and people of the time could not know them.

sentences.zh: 遷比部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Minister of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 以頻從征伐規略之功，進爵壽光侯，加建義將軍。

translations.literal: For repeatedly following campaigns and achievements in strategy, he was advanced to Marquis of Shouguang and given the additional title General Who Establishes Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: For his repeated service on campaign and his achievements in strategy, he was advanced to Marquis of Shouguang and given the additional title General Who Establishes Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 真君末，車駕南伐，將出彭城。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenjun era, the imperial carriage undertook a southern campaign and was about to emerge at Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenjun era, the emperor undertook a southern campaign and was about to advance on Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 劉義隆子安北將軍、徐州刺史、武陵王駿，遣將馬文恭率步騎萬餘至蕭城。

translations.literal: Liu Yilong's son, General Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Xu Province, and Prince of Wuling, Jun, sent the general Ma Wengong with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry to Xiaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yilong's son, the Prince of Wuling, Jun — who held the titles General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xu Province — sent the general Ma Wengong with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry to Xiaocheng.

sentences.zh: 前軍擊破之，文恭走免，執其隊主蒯應。

translations.literal: The vanguard routed them; Wengong fled and escaped, but his squad leader Kuai Ying was captured.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard routed them. Wengong fled and escaped, but his squad leader Kuai Ying was captured.

sentences.zh: 義隆聞大駕南巡，又遣其弟太尉、江夏王義恭率眾赴彭城。

translations.literal: When Yilong heard that the great carriage was touring south, he also sent his younger brother, Grand Commandant and Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, with troops to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Yilong learned that the emperor was touring south, he also sent his younger brother, the Prince of Jiangxia, Yigong — who held the title Grand Commandant — with troops to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 世祖至彭城，登亞父冢以望城內，遣送蒯應至小市門，宣世祖詔，勞問義恭等，[1]并遣自陳蕭城之敗。

translations.literal: When Shizu reached Pengcheng, he ascended the mound of the Second Father to look into the city, sent Kuai Ying to the Lesser Market Gate, proclaimed Shizu's edict, conveyed greetings to Yigong and the others, [1] and also had him describe the defeat at Xiaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu reached Pengcheng, he climbed the mound of the Second Father to look into the city, sent Kuai Ying to the Lesser Market Gate, proclaimed the emperor's edict, conveyed greetings to Yigong and the others, [1] and had him describe the defeat at Xiaocheng.

sentences.zh: 義恭等問應：「魏帝自來以不？

translations.literal: Yigong and the others asked Ying: "Has the Wei emperor come in person or not?"
translations.idiomatic: Yigong and the others asked Ying, "Has the Wei emperor come in person?"

sentences.zh: 」應曰：「自來。

translations.literal: Ying replied: "He has come in person."
translations.idiomatic: Ying replied, "He has come in person."

sentences.zh: 」又問：「今在何處？

translations.literal: They asked again: "Where is he now?"
translations.idiomatic: They asked again, "Where is he now?"

sentences.zh: 」應曰：「在城西南。

translations.literal: Ying replied: "Southwest of the city."
translations.idiomatic: Ying replied, "Southwest of the city."

sentences.zh: 」又問：「士馬多少？

translations.literal: They asked again: "How many troops and horses?"
translations.idiomatic: They asked again, "How many troops and horses are there?"

sentences.zh: 」應曰：「中軍四十餘萬。

translations.literal: Ying replied: "The central army numbers more than four hundred thousand."
translations.idiomatic: Ying replied, "The central army numbers more than four hundred thousand."

sentences.zh: 」駿遣人獻酒二器、甘蔗百梃，并請駱駝。

translations.literal: Jun sent men to present two vessels of wine and a hundred stalks of sugarcane, and also to request camels.
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent men to present two vessels of wine and a hundred stalks of sugarcane, and also to request camels.

sentences.zh: 世祖明旦復登亞父冢，遣孝伯至小市，駿亦遣其長史張暢對孝伯。

translations.literal: The next morning Shizu again ascended the mound of the Second Father and sent Xiaobo to the Lesser Market; Jun also sent his Chief Clerk Zhang Chang to face Xiaobo.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning Shizu again climbed the mound of the Second Father and sent Xiaobo to the Lesser Market. Jun also sent his Chief Clerk Zhang Chang to meet Xiaobo.

sentences.zh: 孝伯遙問暢姓，暢曰：「姓張。

translations.literal: From afar Xiaobo asked Chang his surname; Chang said: "My surname is Zhang."
translations.idiomatic: From a distance Xiaobo asked Chang his surname. Chang said, "My surname is Zhang."

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「是張長史也。

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "That is Chief Clerk Zhang."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "That must be Chief Clerk Zhang."

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「君何得見識？

translations.literal: Chang said: "How did you recognize me?"
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "How did you recognize me?"

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「既涉此境，何容不悉。

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "Having entered this territory, how could I not know you thoroughly?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "Having entered this territory, how could I not know you?"

sentences.zh: 」暢問孝伯曰：「君復何姓？

translations.literal: Chang asked Xiaobo: "And what is your surname?
translations.idiomatic: Chang asked Xiaobo, "And what is your surname?

sentences.zh: 居何官也？

translations.literal: What office do you hold?"
translations.idiomatic: What office do you hold?"

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「我戎行一夫，何足致問。

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "I am but one man in the army — hardly worth asking about.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "I am but one man in the army — hardly worth asking about.

sentences.zh: 然足與君相敵。

translations.literal: Yet I am quite your match."
translations.idiomatic: Yet I am quite your match."

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「主上有詔：『太尉、安北可暫出門，欲與相見，朕亦不攻彭城，何為勞苦將士，城上嚴備？

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "The sovereign has an edict: 'Grand Commandant and General Who Pacifies the North may for a time come outside the gate; he wishes to meet you. I likewise shall not attack Pengcheng — why trouble your officers and men with strict defenses on the walls?'
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "The sovereign has an edict: 'Grand Commandant and General Who Pacifies the North may come outside the gate for a time; he wishes to meet you. I likewise shall not attack Pengcheng — so why trouble your officers and men with strict defenses on the walls?'

sentences.zh: 』今遣賜駱駝及貂裘雜物。

translations.literal: Now he sends camels, sable furs, and various goods as gifts.'"
translations.idiomatic: He now sends camels, sable furs, and various goods as gifts.'"

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「有詔之言，政可施於彼國，何得稱之於此？

translations.literal: Chang said: "Language of an edict may properly be applied in that state — how can it be invoked here?"
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "Language fit for an edict may be used in your state — how can it be invoked here?"

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「卿家太尉、安北，是人臣不？

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "Are your Grand Commandant and General Who Pacifies the North subjects or not?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "Are your Grand Commandant and General Who Pacifies the North subjects or not?"

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「是也。

translations.literal: Chang said: "They are."
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "They are."

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「我朝廷奄有萬國，率土之濱，莫敢不臣，縱為隣國之君，何為不稱詔於隣國之臣？

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "Our court embraces the myriad states; along the shores of the land none dares not submit. Even as sovereign of a neighboring state, why should he not invoke an edict toward subjects of a neighboring state?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "Our court embraces the myriad states; along the shores of the land none dares refuse submission. Even as sovereign of a neighboring state, why should he not speak by edict to subjects of a neighboring state?"

sentences.zh: 」孝伯又問暢曰：「何至忽遽杜門絕橋？

translations.literal: Xiaobo further asked Chang: "Why go so far as hastily to shut the gates and cut the bridges?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo further asked Chang, "Why go so far as to shut the gates and cut the bridges in such haste?"

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「二王以魏帝壁壘未立，將士疲勞，此精甲十萬，人思致命，恐輕相凌踐，故且閉城耳。

translations.literal: Chang said: "The two princes, seeing that the Wei emperor's encampments are not yet established and the troops are weary, with a hundred thousand elite armored men here who all long to give their lives, feared a rash assault — hence for the moment the city is closed."
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "The two princes saw that the Wei emperor's encampments were not yet established and the troops were weary. Here are a hundred thousand elite armored men who all long to give their lives, and they feared a rash assault — so for the moment the city is closed."

sentences.zh: 待休息士馬，然後共治戰場，剋日交戲。

translations.literal: When horses and men have rested, then we shall together set the battlefield and fix a day for contest."
translations.idiomatic: When horses and men have rested, we shall together set the battlefield and fix a day for battle."

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「令行禁止，主將常事，宜當以法裁物，何用發橋杜門？

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "Enforcing orders and prohibiting transgression is the constant duty of a commander-in-chief; one should measure affairs by law — what need to cut bridges and shut gates?
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "Enforcing orders and prohibiting transgression is the constant duty of a commander-in-chief. One should measure affairs by law — what need is there to cut bridges and shut gates?

sentences.zh: 窮城之中，復何以十萬誇大？

translations.literal: Within a besieged city, how can one again boast of a hundred thousand?
translations.idiomatic: Within a besieged city, how can one boast of a hundred thousand?

sentences.zh: 我亦有良馬百萬，復可以此相矜。

translations.literal: We too have a million fine horses — shall we likewise vaunt ourselves with that?"
translations.idiomatic: We too have a million fine horses — shall we boast of that as well?"

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「王侯設險，何但法令而已也。

translations.literal: Chang said: "When lords and princes establish defenses, that is more than mere laws and regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "When lords and princes establish defenses, that is more than mere laws and regulations.

sentences.zh: 我若誇君，當言百萬，所以言十萬者，正是二王左右素所畜養者耳。

translations.literal: If I were to boast to you, I would say a million; the reason I say a hundred thousand is precisely the men the two princes have long kept about them.
translations.idiomatic: If I were to boast to you, I would say a million. The reason I say a hundred thousand is precisely the men the two princes have long kept about them.

sentences.zh: 此城內有數州士庶，工徒營伍猶所未論。

translations.literal: Within this city are people from several provinces — craftsmen, laborers, and garrison troops are still uncounted.
translations.idiomatic: Within this city are people from several provinces — craftsmen, laborers, and garrison troops are still uncounted.

sentences.zh: 我本鬬人，不鬬馬足。

translations.literal: I came to fight men, not to compete in horses.
translations.idiomatic: I came to fight men, not to compete in horses.

sentences.zh: 且冀之北土，馬之所生，君復何以逸足見誇也？

translations.literal: Moreover the northern lands of Ji are where horses are bred — with what fleet steeds do you again boast?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the northern lands of Ji are where horses are bred — with what fleet steeds do you boast?"

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「王侯設險，誠如來言，開閉有常，何為杜塞？

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "Lords and princes establish defenses — truly as you say; opening and closing have their rules — why block and seal?
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "Lords and princes establish defenses — truly as you say. Opening and closing have their rules — why block and seal everything?

sentences.zh: 絕橋之意，義在何也？

translations.literal: As for cutting the bridges — what is the point of that?
translations.idiomatic: As for cutting the bridges — what is the point?

sentences.zh: 此城守君之所習，野戰我之所長，我之恃馬，猶如君之恃城耳。

translations.literal: Siege defense is what you excel at; field battle is what we excel at; our reliance on horses is just like your reliance on walls."
translations.idiomatic: Siege defense is what you excel at; field battle is what we excel at. Our reliance on horses is just like your reliance on walls."

sentences.zh: 」城內有貝思者，[2]嘗至京師，義恭遣視之，思識是孝伯。

translations.literal: Within the city was one Bei Si, [2] who had once been to the capital; Yigong sent him to look and Si recognized that it was Xiaobo.
translations.idiomatic: Within the city was one Bei Si, [2] who had once been to the capital. Yigong sent him to look, and Si recognized Xiaobo.

sentences.zh: 思前問孝伯曰：「李尚書行途有勞。

translations.literal: Si stepped forward and said to Xiaobo: "Minister Li, the journey has been wearying."
translations.idiomatic: Si stepped forward and said to Xiaobo, "Minister Li, the journey must have been wearying."

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「此事應相與共知。

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "This matter ought to be known to us both together."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "This matter ought to be known to us both."

sentences.zh: 」思答曰：「緣共知，所以仰勞。

translations.literal: Si answered: "Because it is known to us both, I offer my respects for your labors."
translations.idiomatic: Si answered, "Because it is known to us both, I offer my respects for your labors."

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「感君至意。」

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "I am moved by your utmost courtesy."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "I am moved by your courtesy."

sentences.zh: 既開門，暢屏人却仗，出受賜物。

translations.literal: Once the gate was opened, Chang dismissed attendants and laid aside weapons, came out and received the gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Once the gate was opened, Chang dismissed his attendants, laid aside his weapons, came out, and received the gifts.

sentences.zh: 孝伯曰：「詔以貂裘賜太尉，駱駝、騾、馬賜安北，蒲萄酒及諸食味當相與同進。

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "The edict bestows sable furs on the Grand Commandant and camels, mules, and horses on the General Who Pacifies the North; grape wine and various delicacies are to be brought in together."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "The edict bestows sable furs on the Grand Commandant and camels, mules, and horses on the General Who Pacifies the North. Grape wine and various delicacies are to be brought in together."

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「二王敬白魏帝，知欲垂見，常願面接，但受命本朝，忝居藩任，人臣無境外之交，故無容私覿。

translations.literal: Chang said: "The two princes respectfully inform the Wei emperor: knowing he wishes to grant an audience, they have always desired a face-to-face meeting, but having received orders from their own court and holding feudal posts in shame, subjects may have no dealings outside their borders — hence there can be no private audience."
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "The two princes respectfully inform the Wei emperor that, knowing he wishes to grant an audience, they have always desired a face-to-face meeting. But having received orders from their own court and holding feudal posts, subjects may have no dealings outside their borders — hence there can be no private audience."

sentences.zh: 」義恭獻皮袴褶一具，駿奉酒二器、甘蔗百梃。

translations.literal: Yigong presented one set of leather trousers and jacket; Jun offered two vessels of wine and a hundred stalks of sugarcane.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong presented one set of leather trousers and jacket. Jun offered two vessels of wine and a hundred stalks of sugarcane.

sentences.zh: 孝伯曰：「又有詔：『太尉、安北，久絕南信，殊當憂悒。

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "There is also an edict: 'Grand Commandant and General Who Pacifies the North, long cut off from news from the south, must be deeply troubled.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "There is also an edict: 'Grand Commandant and General Who Pacifies the North, long cut off from news from the south, must be deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 若欲遣信者，當為護送，脫須騎者，亦當以馬送之。

translations.literal: If you wish to send messengers, we shall escort them; should you need riders, we shall likewise provide horses to deliver them.'"
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to send messengers, we shall escort them. Should you need riders, we shall likewise provide horses to deliver them.'"

sentences.zh: 』」暢曰：「此方間路甚多，使命日夕往復，不復以此勞魏帝也。

translations.literal: Chang said: "On this side there are many byways; messengers come and go day and night — we need not further trouble the Wei emperor with this."
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "On this side there are many byways, and messengers come and go day and night — we need not further trouble the Wei emperor with this."

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「亦知有水路，似為白賊所斷。

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "We know too there is a water route, but it seems cut off by White Bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "We know there is also a water route, but it seems to have been cut off by White Bandits."

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「君著白衣，稱白賊也。

translations.literal: Chang said: "You wear white garments — you are the White Bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "You wear white garments — you are the White Bandits."

sentences.zh: 」孝伯大笑曰：「今之白賊，似異黃巾、赤眉。

translations.literal: Xiaobo laughed heartily: "Today's White Bandits seem unlike the Yellow Turbans and Red Eyebrows."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo laughed heartily and said, "Today's White Bandits seem unlike the Yellow Turbans and Red Eyebrows."

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「黃巾、赤眉，不在江南。

translations.literal: Chang said: "The Yellow Turbans and Red Eyebrows are not in Jiangnan."
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "The Yellow Turbans and Red Eyebrows are not in Jiangnan."

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「雖不在江南，亦不離徐方也。

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "Though not in Jiangnan, they are not far from the Xu region either."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "Though not in Jiangnan, they are not far from the Xu region either."

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「向與安北相聞，何以久而不報？

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "Earlier I exchanged messages with the General Who Pacifies the North — why so long without reply?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "Earlier I exchanged messages with the General Who Pacifies the North — why has there been no reply for so long?"

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「二王貴遠，啟聞為難。

translations.literal: Chang said: "The two princes are of lofty rank and far removed; reporting and inquiry are difficult."
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "The two princes are of lofty rank and far removed; reporting and inquiry are difficult."

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「周公握髮吐餔，二王何獨貴遠？

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "The Duke of Zhou would clench his hair and spit out food in haste — why alone should the two princes be so lofty and remote?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "The Duke of Zhou would clench his hair and spit out his food in haste — why alone should the two princes be so lofty and remote?"

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「握髮吐餐，不謂隣國之人也。

translations.literal: Chang said: "Clenching hair and spitting out food — that is not said of people of a neighboring state."
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "Clenching one's hair and spitting out one's food — that is not said of people of a neighboring state."

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「本邦尚爾，隣國彌應盡恭。

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "If even within one's own state it is so, toward a neighboring state one should all the more show full deference.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "If even within one's own state it is so, toward a neighboring state one should all the more show full deference.

sentences.zh: 且賓至有禮，主人宜以禮接。

translations.literal: Moreover when guests arrive, the host ought to receive them with propriety."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when guests arrive, the host ought to receive them with propriety."

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「昨見眾賓至門，未為有禮。

translations.literal: Chang said: "Yesterday I saw many guests reach the gate — that was hardly propriety."
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "Yesterday I saw many guests reach the gate — that was hardly propriety."

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「非是賓至無禮，直是主人怱怱，無待賓調度耳。

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "It was not that the guests arrived without propriety — simply the host was in haste and did not wait to arrange for the guests."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "It was not that the guests arrived without propriety — the host was simply in haste and did not wait to arrange for the guests."

sentences.zh: 」孝伯又言：「有詔：『程天祚一介常人，誠知非江南之選，近於汝陽，身被九槍，落在溵水，我使牽而出之。

translations.literal: Xiaobo spoke again: "There is an edict: 'Cheng Tianzuo is an ordinary common man and truly no choice man of Jiangnan; near Ruyang he took nine spear wounds and fell into the Yin River — I had him pulled out.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo spoke again: "There is an edict: 'Cheng Tianzuo is an ordinary common man and truly no choice man of Jiangnan. Near Ruyang he took nine spear wounds and fell into the Yin River — I had him pulled out.

sentences.zh: 凡人骨肉分張，並思集聚，聞其弟在此，如何不遣暫出？

translations.literal: Ordinary people, their flesh and bone scattered, all long to reunite; hearing his younger brother is here, why not send him out briefly?
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary people, their flesh and bone scattered, all long to reunite. Hearing his younger brother is here, why not send him out briefly?

sentences.zh: 尋自令反，豈復苟留一人。

translations.literal: Soon I shall let him return — how could I detain a single man wantonly?'"
translations.idiomatic: Soon I shall let him return — how could I detain a single man wantonly?'"

sentences.zh: 』」暢曰：「知欲程天祚兄弟集聚，已勒遣之，但其固辭不往。

translations.literal: Chang said: "Knowing you wish the Cheng Tianzuo brothers to reunite, we have already ordered him sent, but he firmly refuses to go."
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "Knowing you wish the Cheng Tianzuo brothers to reunite, we have already ordered him sent, but he firmly refuses to go."

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「豈有子弟聞其父兄而反不肯相見，此便禽獸之不若。

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "How can there be sons and younger brothers who, hearing of their father and elder brothers, yet refuse to meet — this is not even as good as birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "How can there be sons and younger brothers who, hearing of their father and elder brothers, yet refuse to meet? This is not even as good as birds and beasts.

sentences.zh: 貴土風俗，何至如此。」

translations.literal: What customs of your noble land reach to such a point?"
translations.idiomatic: What customs of your noble land reach to such a point?"

sentences.zh: 世祖又遣賜義恭、駿等氈各一領，鹽各九種，并胡豉。

translations.literal: Shizu again sent gifts of one rug each to Yigong, Jun, and the others, nine kinds of salt each, and fermented bean paste from the north.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu again sent one rug each to Yigong, Jun, and the others, nine kinds of salt each, and fermented bean paste from the north.

sentences.zh: 孝伯曰：「有後詔：『凡此諸鹽，各有所宜。

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "There is a further edict: 'Each of these salts has its proper use.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "There is a further edict: 'Each of these salts has its proper use.

sentences.zh: 白鹽食鹽，主上自食；

translations.literal: White salt and table salt the sovereign eats himself;
translations.idiomatic: White salt and table salt the sovereign eats himself;

sentences.zh: 黑鹽治腹脹氣滿，末之六銖，以酒而服；

translations.literal: black salt treats abdominal distension and fullness of qi — grind six zhu of it and take it with wine;
translations.idiomatic: black salt treats abdominal distension and fullness of qi — grind six zhu of it and take it with wine;

sentences.zh: 胡鹽治目痛；

translations.literal: Hu salt treats eye pain;
translations.idiomatic: Hu salt treats eye pain;

sentences.zh: 戎鹽治諸瘡；

translations.literal: barbarian salt treats various sores;
translations.idiomatic: barbarian salt treats various sores;

sentences.zh: 赤鹽、駁鹽、臭鹽、馬齒鹽四種，並非食鹽。

translations.literal: red salt, variegated salt, foul salt, and horsetooth salt — these four kinds are none of them table salt.
translations.idiomatic: red salt, variegated salt, foul salt, and horsetooth salt — these four kinds are none of them table salt.

sentences.zh: 太尉、安北何不遣人來至朕間？

translations.literal: Grand Commandant and General Who Pacifies the North — why not send someone to my presence?
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant and General Who Pacifies the North — why not send someone to my presence?

sentences.zh: 彼此之情，雖不可盡，要復見朕小大，知朕老少，觀朕為人。

translations.literal: Feelings between us, though they cannot be fully expressed, should at least let you see my stature, know my age, and observe what manner of man I am.'"
translations.idiomatic: Feelings between us, though they cannot be fully expressed, should at least let you see my stature, know my age, and observe what manner of man I am.'"

sentences.zh: 』」暢曰：「魏帝久為往來所具，李尚書親自銜命，不患彼此不盡，故不復遣信。

translations.literal: Chang said: "The Wei emperor has long been fully described in our mutual exchanges; Minister Li himself bears the commission — we need not fear that feelings on both sides are not fully conveyed, hence we do not send a messenger again."
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "The Wei emperor has long been fully described in our mutual exchanges. Minister Li himself bears the commission — we need not fear that feelings on both sides are not fully conveyed, hence we do not send a messenger again."

sentences.zh: 」義恭獻蠟燭十梃，駿獻錦一匹。

translations.literal: Yigong presented ten candles; Jun presented one bolt of brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Yigong presented ten candles. Jun presented one bolt of brocade.

sentences.zh: 孝伯曰：「君南土士人，何為著屩？

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "You are a gentleman of the southern lands — why wear slippers?
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "You are a gentleman of the southern lands — why wear slippers?

sentences.zh: 君而著此，將士云何？

translations.literal: If you wear these, what shall the officers and men do?"
translations.idiomatic: If you wear these, what shall the officers and men do?"

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「士人之言，誠為多愧。

translations.literal: Chang said: "Your words as a gentleman do indeed cause much shame.
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "Your words as a gentleman do indeed cause much shame.

sentences.zh: 但以不武，受命統軍，戎陳之間，不容緩服。

translations.literal: But being no warrior, yet having received orders to command armies, amid the battle array one cannot dress at ease."
translations.idiomatic: But being no warrior, yet having received orders to command armies, amid the battle array one cannot dress at ease."

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「永昌王自頃恒鎮長安，今領精騎八萬直造淮南，壽春亦閉門自固，不敢相禦。

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "Prince of Yongchang has long garrisoned Chang'an; now he leads eighty thousand elite cavalry straight toward Huainan; Shouyang too has shut its gates and holds firm, not daring to oppose.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "The Prince of Yongchang has long garrisoned Chang'an. Now he leads eighty thousand elite cavalry straight toward Huainan. Shouyang too has shut its gates and holds firm, not daring to oppose.

sentences.zh: 向送劉康祖首，彼之所見。

translations.literal: Recently we sent Liu Kangzu's head — that is what they have seen.
translations.idiomatic: Recently we sent Liu Kangzu's head — that is what they have seen.

sentences.zh: 王玄謨甚是所悉，亦是常才耳。

translations.literal: Wang Xuanmo is very well known to us — he too is merely ordinary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuanmo is very well known to us — he too is merely ordinary talent.

sentences.zh: 何意作如此任使，以致奔敗。

translations.literal: Why appoint him to such a role as to end in flight and defeat?
translations.idiomatic: Why appoint him to such a role as to end in flight and defeat?

sentences.zh: 自入境七百餘里，主人竟不能一相拒抗。

translations.literal: Since entering the territory more than seven hundred li, the host has not once been able to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Since entering your territory more than seven hundred li, the host has not once been able to resist.

sentences.zh: 鄒山之險，彼之所憑，前鋒始得接手，崔邪利便爾入穴，將士倒曳出之。

translations.literal: The peril of Mount Zou was their reliance; scarcely had the vanguard joined battle when Cui Xieli went straight into a cave, and the officers and men dragged him out headlong.
translations.idiomatic: The peril of Mount Zou was their reliance. Scarcely had the vanguard joined battle when Cui Xieli went straight into a cave, and the officers and men dragged him out headlong.

sentences.zh: 主上丐其生命，今從在此。

translations.literal: The sovereign spared his life; now he follows us here.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign spared his life, and now he follows us here.

sentences.zh: 復何以輕脫，遣馬文恭至蕭縣，使望風退撓也。

translations.literal: Why again so lightly send Ma Wengong to Xiaoxian, causing him to falter and withdraw at sight of the enemy?
translations.idiomatic: Why again so lightly send Ma Wengong to Xiaoxian, causing him to falter and withdraw at sight of the enemy?

sentences.zh: 彼之民人，甚相忿怨，言清平之時，賦我租帛，至有急難，不能相拯。

translations.literal: The people there are deeply resentful, saying: in times of peace you levied our rents and cloth, yet when crisis came you could not save us."
translations.idiomatic: The people there are deeply resentful, saying that in times of peace you levied their rents and cloth, yet when crisis came you could not save them."

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「知永昌已過淮南。

translations.literal: Chang said: "We know Yongchang has already passed Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "We know Yongchang has already passed Huainan.

sentences.zh: 康祖為其所破，比有信使，無此消息。

translations.literal: Kangzu was defeated by him, but according to recent messengers there is no such news.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzu was defeated by him, but according to recent messengers there is no such news.

sentences.zh: 王玄謨南土偏將，不謂為才，但以其北人，故為前驅引導耳。

translations.literal: Wang Xuanmo is a partial general of the southern lands — not counted as talented, but because he is a northerner he was made vanguard and guide.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xuanmo is a partial general of the southern lands — not counted as talented, but because he is a northerner he was made vanguard and guide.

sentences.zh: 大軍未至，而河冰向合，玄謨量宜反旆，未為失算，但因夜回歸，致戎馬驚亂耳。

translations.literal: The great army had not yet arrived and the river ice was about to close; Xuanmo judged it fit to turn back — that was no miscalculation, but the night retreat caused horses and troops to panic and scatter.
translations.idiomatic: The great army had not yet arrived and the river ice was about to close. Xuanmo judged it fit to turn back — that was no miscalculation, but the night retreat caused horses and troops to panic and scatter.

sentences.zh: 我家懸瓠小城，陳憲小將，魏帝傾國攻圍，累旬不克。

translations.literal: Our little town of Xuanhuo — the minor general Chen Xian — the Wei emperor threw the whole state's force against it in siege for many weeks without taking it.
translations.idiomatic: Our little town of Xuanhuo — the minor general Chen Xian — the Wei emperor threw the whole state's force against it in siege for many weeks without taking it.

sentences.zh: 胡盛之偏裨小帥，眾無三旅，始濟翮水，[3]魏國君臣奔散，僅得免脫。

translations.literal: Hu Shengzhi, a petty subordinate commander with fewer than three regiments, had just crossed the Yi River [3] when the Wei state's lords and ministers scattered in flight and barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shengzhi, a petty subordinate commander with fewer than three regiments, had just crossed the Yi River [3] when the Wei state's lords and ministers scattered in flight and barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 滑臺之師，無所多愧。

translations.literal: As for the army at Huatai — there is little to be ashamed of.
translations.idiomatic: As for the army at Huatai — there is little to be ashamed of.

sentences.zh: 鄒山小戍，雖有微險，河畔之民，多是新附，始慕政化，姦盜未息，示使崔邪利撫之而已。

translations.literal: The little fort at Mount Zou, though it had slight strategic advantage, had riverside people mostly newly submitted, just beginning to admire civilized rule while theft and banditry had not ceased — they merely showed Cui Xieli to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: The little fort at Mount Zou, though it had slight strategic advantage, had riverside people mostly newly submitted, just beginning to admire civilized rule while theft and banditry had not ceased — they merely sent Cui Xieli to pacify them.

sentences.zh: [4]今雖陷沒，何損於國。

translations.literal: [4] Though it has now fallen, what loss is that to the state?
translations.idiomatic: [4] Though it has now fallen, what loss is that to the state?

sentences.zh: 魏帝自以十萬之師而制一崔邪利，乃復足言也？

translations.literal: The Wei emperor himself needed a hundred-thousand-man army to take one Cui Xieli — is that even worth mentioning?
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor himself needed a hundred-thousand-man army to take one Cui Xieli — is that even worth mentioning?

sentences.zh: 近聞蕭縣百姓並依山險，聊遣馬文恭以十隊迎之耳。

translations.literal: Recently we heard the people of Xiaoxian all cling to mountain defiles — we merely sent Ma Wengong with ten squads to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Recently we heard the people of Xiaoxian all cling to mountain defiles — we merely sent Ma Wengong with ten squads to receive them.

sentences.zh: 文恭前以三隊出，還走彼大營。

translations.literal: Wengong earlier went out with three squads and returned fleeing to their great camp.
translations.idiomatic: Wengong earlier went out with three squads and returned fleeing to their great camp.

sentences.zh: 嵇玄敬以百舸至留城，魏軍奔敗。

translations.literal: Ji Xuanjing with a hundred ships reached Liucheng — the Wei army fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Xuanjing with a hundred ships reached Liucheng — the Wei army fled in defeat.

sentences.zh: 輕敵致此，亦非所卹。

translations.literal: Contempt for the enemy brought this — it is not what we regret.
translations.idiomatic: Contempt for the enemy brought this — it is not what we regret.

sentences.zh: 王境人民，列居河畔，二國交兵，當互加撫養。

translations.literal: The people of the royal domains dwell along the river — when two states clash in arms, each side ought to extend mutual care.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the royal domains dwell along the river — when two states clash in arms, each side ought to extend mutual care.

sentences.zh: 而魏師入境，事生意外，官不負民，民亦何怨。

translations.literal: But when the Wei army entered the territory, matters arose beyond expectation; the officials did not fail the people — why should the people resent?
translations.idiomatic: But when the Wei army entered the territory, matters arose beyond expectation. The officials did not fail the people — why should the people resent?

sentences.zh: 知入境七百里，無相捍拒，此自上由太尉神算，次在武陵聖略，軍國之要，雖不預聞，然用兵有機間，亦不容相語。

translations.literal: Knowing you penetrated seven hundred li without meeting resistance — this from above rests on the Grand Commandant's divine calculation, next on the Prince of Wuling's sagely strategy; the essentials of army and state, though not heard in advance, yet in employing troops there are secret designs that cannot be shared."
translations.idiomatic: Knowing you penetrated seven hundred li without meeting resistance — this from above rests on the Grand Commandant's divine calculation, next on the Prince of Wuling's sagely strategy. The essentials of army and state, though not heard in advance, yet in employing troops there are secret designs that cannot be shared."

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「君藉此虛談，支離相對，可謂遁辭知其所窮。

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "You rely on this empty talk, matching me with fractured replies — one may call it evasive speech that shows where you are cornered.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "You rely on this empty talk, matching me with fractured replies — one may call it evasive speech that shows where you are cornered.

sentences.zh: 且主上當不圍此城，自率眾軍直造瓜步。

translations.literal: Moreover the sovereign will not besiege this city; he will himself lead the hosts straight to Guabu.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the sovereign will not besiege this city. He will himself lead the hosts straight to Guabu.

sentences.zh: 南事若辦，城故不待攻圍；

translations.literal: If affairs in the south succeed, the city naturally need not await siege;
translations.idiomatic: If affairs in the south succeed, the city naturally need not await siege;

sentences.zh: 南行不捷，彭城亦非所欲也。

translations.literal: if the southern advance is not victorious, Pengcheng is not what he desires either.
translations.idiomatic: if the southern advance is not victorious, Pengcheng is not what he desires either.

sentences.zh: 我今當南，欲飲馬江湖耳。

translations.literal: I now go south — I mean only to water my horses in the rivers and lakes."
translations.idiomatic: I now go south — I mean only to water my horses in the rivers and lakes."

sentences.zh: 」暢曰：「去留之事，自適彼懷。

translations.literal: Chang said: "Matters of going and staying suit your own wish.
translations.idiomatic: Chang said, "Matters of going and staying suit your own wish.

sentences.zh: 若魏帝遂得飲馬長江，便為無復天道。

translations.literal: If the Wei emperor should truly water his horses in the Yangtze, that would mean Heaven's Way no longer exists."
translations.idiomatic: If the Wei emperor should truly water his horses in the Yangtze, that would mean Heaven's Way no longer exists."

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「自北而南，實惟人化，飲馬長江，豈獨天道？

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "From north to south is truly human transformation; watering horses in the Yangtze — is that solely Heaven's Way?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "From north to south is truly human transformation. Watering horses in the Yangtze — is that solely Heaven's Way?"

sentences.zh: 」暢將還城，謂孝伯曰：「冀蕩定有期，相見無遠。

translations.literal: As Chang was about to return to the city, he said to Xiaobo: "I hope pacification will come in due time; our meeting again will not be far off.
translations.idiomatic: As Chang was about to return to the city, he said to Xiaobo, "I hope pacification will come in due time. Our meeting again will not be far off.

sentences.zh: 君若得還宋朝，今為相識之始。

translations.literal: If you should return to the Song court, today is the beginning of our acquaintance."
translations.idiomatic: If you should return to the Song court, today is the beginning of our acquaintance."

sentences.zh: 」孝伯曰：「今當先至建業以待君耳。

translations.literal: Xiaobo said: "I shall now go first to Jiankang to await you.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo said, "I shall now go first to Jiankang to await you.

sentences.zh: 恐爾日君與二王面縛請罪，不暇為容。」

translations.literal: I fear that day you and the two princes will be bound facing forward to beg pardon, with no leisure for pleasantries."
translations.idiomatic: I fear that day you and the two princes will be bound facing forward to beg pardon, with no leisure for pleasantries."

sentences.zh: 孝伯風容閑雅，應答如流，暢及左右甚相嗟歎。

translations.literal: Xiaobo's bearing was leisurely and refined, his replies fluent as a stream; Chang and those beside him greatly sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo's bearing was leisurely and refined, his replies fluent as a stream. Chang and those beside him greatly sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 世祖大喜，進爵宣城公。

translations.literal: Shizu was greatly pleased and advanced his noble rank to Duke of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu was greatly pleased and advanced his noble rank to Duke of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 興安二年，出為使持節、散騎常侍、平西將軍、秦州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xing'an he was sent out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xing'an he was sent out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Regular Attendant, General Who Pacifies the West, and Inspector of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: [5]太安五年卒，高宗甚悼惜之。

translations.literal: [5] In the fifth year of Tai'an he died; Emperor Gaozong deeply mourned and grieved for him.
translations.idiomatic: [5] In the fifth year of Tai'an he died. Emperor Gaozong deeply mourned and grieved for him.

sentences.zh: 贈鎮南大將軍、定州刺史，諡曰文昭公。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the titles Grand General Who Guards the South and Inspector of Ding Province; his posthumous name was Duke Wen Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Grand General Who Guards the South and Inspector of Ding Province, and given the posthumous name Duke Wen Zhao.

sentences.zh: 孝伯體度恢雅，明達政事，朝野貴賤，咸推重之。

translations.literal: Xiaobo's stature and manner were magnanimous and refined; he was clear and penetrating in governance; nobles and commoners, court and country, all esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo's stature and manner were magnanimous and refined. He was clear and penetrating in governance, and nobles and commoners, court and country, all esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 恭宗曾啟世祖廣徵俊秀，世祖曰：「朕有一孝伯，足治天下，何用多為？

translations.literal: Emperor Gongzong once urged Shizu to broadly summon outstanding talent; Shizu said: "I have one Xiaobo — enough to govern the realm; why need many?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gongzong once urged Shizu to broadly summon outstanding talent. Shizu said, "I have one Xiaobo — enough to govern the realm. Why need many?

sentences.zh: 假復求訪，此人輩亦何可得。

translations.literal: Even if one sought them out, men of this sort — how could they be obtained?"
translations.idiomatic: Even if one sought them out, men of this sort — how could they be obtained?"

sentences.zh: 」其見賞如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 性方慎忠厚，每朝廷大事有不足，必手自書表，切言陳諫，或不從者，至於再三。

translations.literal: By nature he was upright, cautious, and loyal; whenever great affairs of court fell short, he necessarily wrote memorials in his own hand and spoke forthrightly in remonstrance; if not heeded, he would do so twice and thrice.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was upright, cautious, and loyal. Whenever great affairs of court fell short, he necessarily wrote memorials in his own hand and spoke forthrightly in remonstrance. If not heeded, he would do so twice and thrice.

sentences.zh: 削滅稿草，家人不見。

translations.literal: He destroyed draft copies; his family did not see them.
translations.idiomatic: He destroyed draft copies, and his family did not see them.

sentences.zh: 公庭論議，常引綱紀，或有言事者，孝伯恣其所陳，假有是非，終不抑折。

translations.literal: In court discussion he always invoked fundamental principles; when someone spoke on affairs, Xiaobo let them state all they wished; even if there were right and wrong, he never suppressed or cut short.
translations.idiomatic: In court discussion he always invoked fundamental principles. When someone spoke on affairs, Xiaobo let them state all they wished. Even if there were right and wrong, he never suppressed or cut short.

sentences.zh: 及見世祖，言其所長，初不隱人姓名以為己善，故衣冠之士，服其雅正。

translations.literal: When he saw Shizu, he spoke of others' strengths; he never concealed people's names to claim credit for himself — hence the gentry admired his refined integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw Shizu, he spoke of others' strengths. He never concealed people's names to claim credit for himself — hence the gentry admired his refined integrity.

sentences.zh: 自崔浩誅後，軍國之謀，咸出孝伯。

translations.literal: After Cui Hao was executed, military and state counsel all issued from Xiaobo.
translations.idiomatic: After Cui Hao was executed, military and state counsel all issued from Xiaobo.

sentences.zh: 世祖寵眷有亞於浩，亦以宰輔遇之。

translations.literal: Shizu's favor toward him was second only to Hao's; he was also treated as a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu's favor toward him was second only to Hao's, and he was also treated as a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 獻替補闕，其迹不見，時人莫得而知也。

translations.literal: His counsel in reform and his rectification of omissions left no visible trace; people of the time could not know them.
translations.idiomatic: His counsel in reform and his rectification of omissions left no visible trace, and people of the time could not know them.

sentences.zh: 卒之日，遠近哀傷焉。

translations.literal: On the day he died, far and near grieved.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he died, far and near grieved.

sentences.zh: 孝伯美名，聞於遐邇，李彪使於江南，蕭賾謂之曰：「孝伯於卿遠近？

translations.literal: Xiaobo's fine reputation was heard in distant regions; when Li Biao was envoy to Jiangnan, Xiao Ze said to him: "Is Xiaobo far from you or near?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo's fine reputation was heard in distant regions. When Li Biao was envoy to Jiangnan, Xiao Ze said to him, "Is Xiaobo far from you or near?"

sentences.zh: 」其為遠人所知若此。

translations.literal: Such was the extent to which distant people knew of him.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the extent to which distant people knew of him.

sentences.zh: 孝伯妻崔賾女，高明婦人，生一子元顯。

translations.literal: Xiaobo's wife was a daughter of Cui Zhen, a capable woman; she bore one son, Yuan Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo's wife was a daughter of Cui Zhen, a capable woman. She bore one son, Yuan Xian.

sentences.zh: 崔氏卒後，納翟氏，不以為妻也。

translations.literal: After the Cui clan lady died, he took the Zhai clan lady but did not make her his wife.
translations.idiomatic: After the Lady Cui died, he took the Lady Zhai but did not make her his wife.

sentences.zh: 憎忌元顯。

translations.literal: She hated and envied Yuan Xian.
translations.idiomatic: She hated and envied Yuan Xian.

sentences.zh: 後遇劫，元顯見害，世云翟氏所為也。

translations.literal: Later during a robbery Yuan Xian was killed; the world said it was the work of the Zhai clan lady.
translations.idiomatic: Later, during a robbery, Yuan Xian was killed. The world said it was the work of the Lady Zhai.

sentences.zh: 元顯志氣甚高，為時人所傷惜。

translations.literal: Yuan Xian's spirit and resolve were very lofty; people of the time mourned and grieved for him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Xian's spirit and resolve were very lofty, and people of the time mourned and grieved for him.

sentences.zh: 翟氏二子，安民、安上，並有風度。

translations.literal: The Zhai clan lady's two sons, Anmin and Anshang, both had fine bearing.
translations.idiomatic: The Lady Zhai's two sons, Anmin and Anshang, both had fine bearing.

sentences.zh: 安民，襲爵壽光侯，司徒司馬。

translations.literal: Anmin inherited the marquisate of Shouguang and served as Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Anmin inherited the marquisate of Shouguang and served as Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Education.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈郢州刺史。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously given the title Inspector of Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, he was posthumously appointed Inspector of Ying Province.

sentences.zh: 無子，爵除。

translations.literal: He had no son; the noble rank was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: He had no son, and the noble rank was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 安上，鉅鹿太守，亦早卒。

translations.literal: Anshang was Administrator of Julu and also died young.
translations.idiomatic: Anshang was Administrator of Julu and also died young.

sentences.zh: 安民弟豹子。

translations.literal: Anmin's younger brother Baozi.
translations.idiomatic: Anmin's younger brother was Baozi.

sentences.zh: 正光三年上書曰：

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhengguang he submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhengguang he submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 竊惟庸勳賞勞，有國恒典；

translations.literal: I reflect that rewarding meritorious service is the constant precedent of a state;
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that rewarding meritorious service is the constant precedent of a state;

sentences.zh: 興滅繼絕，哲后所先。

translations.literal: reviving what is extinguished and continuing what is broken off is what a sage sovereign puts first.
translations.idiomatic: reviving what is extinguished and continuing what is broken off is what a sage sovereign puts first.

sentences.zh: 是以積德累忠，春秋許宥十世；

translations.literal: Therefore, accumulating virtue and piling up loyalty—the Spring and Autumn Annals allowed pardon across ten generations;
translations.idiomatic: Thus it is that when virtue is heaped up and loyalty accumulated, the Spring and Autumn Annals permitted grace to extend across ten generations;

sentences.zh: 立功著節，河山誓其永久。

translations.literal: establishing merit and displaying integrity—the rivers and mountains pledged them forever.
translations.idiomatic: when merit was won and integrity made manifest, the rivers and mountains themselves were sworn to preserve the reward forever.

sentences.zh: 伏惟世祖太武皇帝，英叡自天，籠罩日域，東清遼海，西定玉門，凌滅漠北，飲馬江水。

translations.literal: I humbly consider Emperor Shizu the Grand Martial Emperor: sage brilliance from Heaven, covering the sun's domain, clearing the eastern seas, settling the Jade Gate in the west, sweeping away the northern deserts, watering horses at the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly reflect that Emperor Shizu the Grand Martial Emperor, with sage brilliance granted by Heaven, cast his shadow over the entire realm: he cleared the eastern seas, secured the Jade Gate in the west, swept the northern deserts, and watered his horses at the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 臣亡父故尚書、宣城公先臣孝伯，冥基感會，邀幸昌辰，綢繆幃幄，繾綣侍從，廟算嘉謀、每蒙顧採。

translations.literal: My deceased father, the former Minister of Works and Duke of Xuancheng, the late subject Xiaobo—by a hidden foundation and responsive fortune, was invited into an auspicious age, closely bound within the inner curtain, intimately attendant at the side; for every strategic counsel from the temple calculations he repeatedly received the emperor's thoughtful selection.
translations.idiomatic: My late father, the former Minister of Works and Duke of Xuancheng, your subject Xiaobo, was drawn by hidden merit and fortunate timing into an age of glory. He served close within the imperial curtain, intimate in attendance; whenever plans were weighed in the temple, his counsel was chosen again and again.

sentences.zh: 于時儲后監國，奏請徵賢，詔報曰：「朕有一孝伯，足以治天下，何用多為？

translations.literal: At that time the crown prince was overseeing the state and submitted a memorial requesting the recruitment of worthies. The edict replied: "I have one Xiaobo—that is enough to govern all under Heaven. What need for more?
translations.idiomatic: At that time the crown prince was regent and memorialized the throne to summon men of talent. The imperial reply came: "I already have Xiaobo—he is enough to govern the realm. Why summon more?"

sentences.zh: 」其見委遇，乃至於此。

translations.literal: " The degree of his commission and favor reached even to this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the depth of the trust and favor shown him.

sentences.zh: 是用寵以元、凱，爵以公侯，詔冊曰：「江陽之巡，奇謀屢進，六師大捷，亦有勳焉。

translations.literal: Therefore he was favored with the rank of Origin and Triumph, ennobled as duke or marquis. The edict and patent said: "At the Jiangyang campaign, novel stratagems were repeatedly submitted; in the great victory of the six armies, he too had merit.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was honored with the highest ministerial rank and ennobled a duke or marquis. The patent read: "On the Jiangyang expedition his ingenious plans were offered again and again; in the great triumph of the six armies he too had a share of the achievement."

sentences.zh: 」出內勤王，寵遇隆厚，方開大賞，而世祖登遐。

translations.literal: " Serving within and without with diligence for the throne, his favor and treatment were generous and thick; just as great rewards were about to open, Emperor Shizu passed away.
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace and beyond it he served the throne with tireless loyalty, and the honors heaped upon him were great. Just as a grand reward was about to be granted, Emperor Shizu departed this life.

sentences.zh: 梓宮始遷，外任名岳。

translations.literal: When the imperial coffin was first moved, he was sent on external assignment to a renowned commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial coffin was first borne away, he was posted to a distinguished frontier commandery.

sentences.zh: 高宗沖年纂運，未及追敍。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong succeeded at a young age and had not yet had time to pursue retrospective honors.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong came to the throne in his youth and had not yet had occasion to grant retrospective honors.

sentences.zh: 臣行舛百靈，先臣棄世，微績未甄，誠志長奪，搢紳僉傷早世，朝野咸哀不永。

translations.literal: My conduct has gone wrong among all spirits; my late father departed this world; his slight achievements were never assessed; his sincere intent was forever cut short; the gentry all lamented his early death; court and countryside alike mourned his brief span.
translations.idiomatic: My own life has gone astray before heaven and earth; my late father has left the world; his modest achievements were never fully recognized, his earnest devotion cut short forever. The gentry grieved that he died too soon; court and countryside alike mourned that his years were too few.

sentences.zh: 臣亡兄襲，無子封除。

translations.literal: My deceased elder brother Xi inherited, but had no son and the fief was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: My late elder brother Xi succeeded to the title, but left no son, and the enfeoffment was abolished.

sentences.zh: 永惟宗構，五情崩圮。

translations.literal: Forever contemplating the ancestral structure, the five emotions collapsed like a wall.
translations.idiomatic: When I think forever on the ancestral line, all five emotions within me crumble like a wall.

sentences.zh: 先臣榮寵前朝，勳書王府，同之常倫，爵封堙墜，準古量今，實深荼苦。

translations.literal: My late father received glory and favor in the previous reign; his achievements were recorded in the princely archives; compared with ordinary norms, rank and fief were buried and fallen; measured against antiquity and weighed against the present, truly deeply bitter as wormwood.
translations.idiomatic: My late father was honored in the previous reign and his deeds were entered in the royal archives; yet by ordinary rule his rank and fief have sunk into oblivion. Measured against ancient precedent and weighed against our own age, the bitterness is truly unbearable.

sentences.zh: 竊惟朝例：廣川王遵、太原公元大曹等，並以勳重先朝，世絕繼祀，或以傍親，或聽弟襲，皆傳河山之功，垂不世之賞。

translations.literal: I have observed the court's precedents: Prince Guangchuan Zun, Yuantuogong Yuanda Cao, and others all, because their merit was weighty in the former dynasty and their line died out with none to continue the sacrifices, either through collateral kin or by allowing younger brothers to inherit—all transmitted the achievement of rivers and mountains, extending an unworldly reward.
translations.idiomatic: I have reviewed the court's precedents: Prince Guangchuan Zun, Yuantuogong Yuanda Cao, and others, because their merit in the former dynasty was great and their line ended with no heir to the sacrifices, were allowed succession through collateral kin or through younger brothers—all preserving the achievement sworn by river and mountain, and passing down rewards unmatched in their age.

sentences.zh: 況先臣在蒙委任，[6]運籌幃帟，勳著於中，聲傳於外。

translations.literal: How much more so when my late father received the trust of commission, [6] strategizing in the inner tent—his merit shown within, his renown transmitted without!
translations.idiomatic: How much more so in the case of my late father, who was entrusted with command, [6] plotted strategy within the command tent, whose merit was manifest at court and whose fame resounded abroad!

sentences.zh: 事等功均，今古無易。

translations.literal: The deeds equal and the merit balanced—from antiquity to today nothing changes.
translations.idiomatic: The deeds were equal and the merit comparable; from antiquity to the present the principle has not changed.

sentences.zh: 是以漢賞信布，裁重良平；

translations.literal: Therefore Han rewarded Xin and Bu with weights as heavy as Liang and Ping;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Han rewarded Han Xin and Ying Bu with honors as weighty as those given Liang and Ping;

sentences.zh: 魏酬張徐，不棄荀郭。

translations.literal: Wei compensated Zhang and Xu, not abandoning Xun and Guo.
translations.idiomatic: Wei repaid Zhang and Xu and did not cast aside Xun and Guo.

sentences.zh: 今數族追賞於先朝之世，先臣絕封於聖明之時，瞻流顧侶，存亡永恨。

translations.literal: Now many clans receive retrospective rewards from the former dynasty's era, while my late father's fief is cut off in the sage-emperor's time—looking to those of the same stream and turning to companions, living and dead alike forever grievance.
translations.idiomatic: Now other clans receive retrospective honors from the age of the former dynasty, while my late father's fief is extinguished in this sage reign. Looking to those who shared his path and turning to his peers, the living and the dead alike are left with everlasting regret.

sentences.zh: 竊見正始中，爰發存亡之詔，褒賢報功之旨。

translations.literal: I have seen that in the Zhengshi era there issued an edict concerning the living and the dead, with the purpose of honoring the worthy and repaying merit.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen that in the Zhengshi era an edict was issued touching the living and the dead alike, with the intent of honoring the worthy and repaying merit.

sentences.zh: 熙平元年，故任城王澄所請十事，復新前澤，成一時之盛事，垂曠代之茂典，凡在纓紱，誰不感慶？

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiping, the former Prince of Rencheng Cheng's ten requested matters restored the former beneficence, forming a great affair of the age, a splendid canon extending across generations—who among those wearing cap and sash was not moved to rejoice?
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiping, the ten petitions of the former Prince of Rencheng Cheng revived former grace, creating a great event of the age and a splendid statute for generations to come. Who among those girded with cap and sash did not rejoice?

sentences.zh: 蓋以奬勸來今，垂範萬古。

translations.literal: Surely it was to encourage and exhort those to come, to hand down a model for ten thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: Surely this was meant to encourage those yet to come and to hand down a model for ten thousand ages.

sentences.zh: 且劉氏偽書，翻流上國，尋其訕謗，百無一實，前後使人，不書姓字，亦無名爵。

translations.literal: Moreover the Liu clan's spurious book circulates in our superior state; examining its slanders, not one in a hundred is true; those sent before and after wrote no surnames or given names, nor any official rank.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the spurious history of the Liu clan circulates in our realm. Examine its slanders and not one claim in a hundred is true. Its envoys, past and present, give neither surname nor given name, nor any official title.

sentences.zh: 至於張暢傳中，略敍先臣對問，雖改脫略盡，自欲矜高，然逸韻難虧，猶見稱載，非直存益於時，沒亦有彰國美。

translations.literal: As for in Zhang Chang's biography, he briefly recounts my late father's responses in audience—though the alterations and omissions have nearly stripped it bare, since he himself wished to aggrandize his height, yet the lingering elegance is hard to diminish and he is still seen praised and recorded—not only that while alive it benefited the times, but even after death also glorified the state's beauty.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhang Chang's biography, my late father's replies at court are briefly recorded. Though the text has been altered and pared away almost to nothing, and though Zhang sought to elevate himself, the lingering force of the exchange cannot be erased; he is still cited with praise. This not only benefited the age while my father lived, but even after death brought glory to the state.

sentences.zh: 乞覽此書，昭然可見。

translations.literal: I beg that this book be examined—it is clearly visible.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to read that book—the truth is plain to see.

sentences.zh: 則微微衰構，重起一朝，先臣潛魂，結草於千載矣。

translations.literal: Then the faintly declining structure would be raised again in a single court; my late father's hidden soul would repay with tied grass across a thousand years!
translations.idiomatic: Then this faintly failing line would rise again in a single reign, and my late father's hidden spirit would repay the debt with tied grass a thousand years hence!

sentences.zh: 卒不得襲。

translations.literal: In the end they did not obtain inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the petition was denied and the line was not restored.

sentences.zh: 孝伯兄祥，字元善。

translations.literal: Xiaobo's elder brother Xiang, courtesy name Yuanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaobo's elder brother Xiang, whose courtesy name was Yuanshan.

sentences.zh: 學傳家業，鄉黨宗之。

translations.literal: He inherited and transmitted the family's scholarly vocation; the village and clan looked up to him.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited the family tradition of scholarship, and his village and clan held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 世祖詔州郡舉賢良，祥應貢，對策合旨，除中書博士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu ordered the provinces and commanderies to recommend worthy and upright men, Xiang responded to the tribute; his written responses accorded with the intent and he was appointed Palace Library Erudite.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu ordered the provinces and commanderies to recommend worthy and upright men, Xiang presented himself. His written answers accorded with the court's intent, and he was appointed Erudite of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 時南土未賓，世祖親駕，遣尚書韓元興率眾出青州，以祥為軍司。

translations.literal: At that time the southern lands had not yet submitted; Emperor Shizu personally led the campaign and dispatched Minister of Works Han Yuanying to lead troops out of Qing Province, with Xiang as army aide.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the south had not yet submitted. Emperor Shizu led the campaign in person and dispatched Minister of Works Han Yuanying with an army from Qing Province, appointing Xiang army aide.

sentences.zh: 略地至于陳汝，淮北之民詣軍降者七千餘戶，遷之於兗豫之南，置淮陽郡以撫之，拜祥為太守，加綏遠將軍，流民歸之者萬餘家，勸課農桑，百姓安業。

translations.literal: He pushed the frontier to Chen and Ru; over seven thousand households north of the Huai submitted to the army and were moved south of Yan and Yu; Huaiyang commandery was established to settle them; Xiang was appointed governor, given the additional title General Pacifying the Distance; over ten thousand households of displaced people returned; he encouraged sericulture; the people found secure livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced as far as Chen and Ru. More than seven thousand households north of the Huai came to the army and surrendered; they were resettled south of Yan and Yu, and Huaiyang Commandery was established to settle them. Xiang was made governor and given the additional title General Pacifying the Distance. More than ten thousand refugee households returned; he encouraged farming and sericulture, and the people lived in peace.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘉之，賜以衣馬。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu commended him and bestowed clothing and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu praised him and bestowed robes and horses.

sentences.zh: 遷河間太守，有威恩之稱。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be Governor of Hejian, with a reputation for both authority and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Governor of Hejian, where he won a reputation for combining authority with kindness.

sentences.zh: 太安中，徵拜中書侍郎，民有千餘，上書乞留數年，高宗不許。

translations.literal: In the Tai'an era he was summoned and appointed Palace Attendant; over a thousand people submitted a memorial asking that he be retained several years; Emperor Gaozong did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tai'an era he was summoned to the post of Palace Attendant. More than a thousand people submitted a memorial asking that he be kept several years longer, but Emperor Gaozong did not agree.

sentences.zh: 卒官，追贈定州刺史、平棘子，諡曰憲。

translations.literal: He died in office; posthumously ennobled as Governor of Ding Province, Baron of Pingji; posthumous title Xian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office. Posthumously he was ennobled Governor of Ding Province and Baron of Pingji, with the posthumous name Constitutional.

sentences.zh: 子安世，[7]幼而聰悟。

translations.literal: His son Anshi, [7] intelligent and perceptive from childhood.
translations.idiomatic: His son Anshi [7] was clever and quick-witted from childhood.

sentences.zh: 興安二年，高宗引見侍郎、博士之子，簡其秀儁者欲為中書學生。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xing'an, Emperor Gaozong summoned the sons of Palace Attendants and Erudites, selecting the outstanding among them to serve as Palace Library students.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xing'an, Emperor Gaozong summoned the sons of Palace Attendants and Erudites and chose the most gifted among them to become students of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 安世年十一，高宗見其尚小，引問之。

translations.literal: Anshi was eleven; Emperor Gaozong saw he was still young and summoned him for questioning.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi was eleven. Emperor Gaozong thought him still too young and called him forward to question him.

sentences.zh: 安世陳說父祖，甚有次第，即以為學生。

translations.literal: Anshi set forth his father and forebears with excellent order and was immediately made a student.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi described his father and ancestors in excellent order and was immediately enrolled as a student.

sentences.zh: 高宗每幸國學，恒獨被引問。

translations.literal: Whenever Emperor Gaozong visited the National University, Anshi alone was invariably summoned for questioning.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Emperor Gaozong visited the National University, Anshi alone was always singled out for questioning.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「汝但守此至大，不慮不富貴。

translations.literal: The edict said: "You need only keep to this greatest principle—no need to worry about not being rich and noble.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Hold fast to this supreme talent, and you need never fear that wealth and rank will not come."

sentences.zh: 」居父憂以孝聞。

translations.literal: " During mourning for his father he was renowned for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning for his father he became known for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 天安初，拜中散，以溫敏敬慎，顯祖親愛之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tian'an he was appointed Palace Cadet; for his warmth, quick wit, respect, and prudence Emperor Xianzu held him in special affection.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Tian'an era he was appointed Palace Cadet. Warm, quick, respectful, and careful, he won the special favor of Emperor Xianzu.

sentences.zh: 累遷主客令。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director of Guests.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated promotions to Director of Guests.

sentences.zh: 蕭賾使劉纘朝貢，安世美容貌，善舉止，纘等自相謂曰：「不有君子，其能國乎？

translations.literal: When Xiao Ze sent Liu Zuan to pay court tribute, Anshi had a fine countenance and bearing; Zuan and the others said to one another: "Were it not for a gentleman, could the state stand?
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Ze sent Liu Zuan to pay tribute at court, Anshi had a handsome face and graceful bearing. Zuan and his companions said to one another, "Without such gentlemen, how could a state endure?"

sentences.zh: 」纘等呼安世為典客，安世曰：「三代不共禮，五帝各異樂，安足以亡秦之官，稱於上國。

translations.literal: " Zuan and the others called Anshi "Director of Ceremonies"; Anshi said: "The Three Dynasties did not share the same rites; the Five Emperors each had different music—how can an office of the fallen Qin be used as a title in a superior state.
translations.idiomatic: " Zuan and the others addressed Anshi as "Director of Ceremonies." Anshi replied, "The Three Dynasties did not share one ritual code; the Five Emperors each had different music. How can a title from the fallen Qin be used to address an envoy of a superior state?"

sentences.zh: 」纘曰：「世異之號，凡有幾也？

translations.literal: " Zuan said: "How many kinds of titles change with the age?
translations.idiomatic: " Zuan asked, "How many such titles have changed with the ages?"

sentences.zh: 」安世曰：「周謂掌客，秦改典客，漢名鴻臚，今曰主客。

translations.literal: " Anshi said: "Zhou called it Director of Guests; Qin changed it to Director of Ceremonies; Han named it Grand Master of Ceremonies; today it is called Director of Guests.
translations.idiomatic: " Anshi said, "Zhou called the office Director of Guests; Qin changed it to Director of Ceremonies; Han named it Grand Master of Ceremonies; today it is Director of Guests."

sentences.zh: 君等不欲影響文武，而殷勤亡秦。

translations.literal: You gentlemen do not wish to trace back to King Wen and King Wu, yet are so earnest about the fallen Qin.
translations.idiomatic: "You are unwilling to invoke the Zhou of King Wen and King Wu, yet so eager to borrow a Qin title from a fallen dynasty."

sentences.zh: 」纘又指方山曰：「此山去燕然遠近？

translations.literal: " Zuan also pointed to Mount Fang and said: "How far is this mountain from Yanran?
translations.idiomatic: " Zuan also pointed to Mount Fang and asked, "How far is this mountain from Yanran?"

sentences.zh: 」安世曰：「亦由石頭之於番禺耳。

translations.literal: " Anshi said: "It is like the distance from Mount Stone to Panyu.
translations.idiomatic: " Anshi replied, "About as far as Mount Stone is from Panyu."

sentences.zh: 」國家有江南使至，多出藏內珍物，令都下富室好容服者貨之，令使任情交易。

translations.literal: When envoys came from the south, the state often produced rare treasures from the palace stores and had the wealthy of the capital who liked fine dress purchase them, allowing the envoys to trade as they pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When envoys arrived from the south, the court often brought out rare goods from the palace stores and had wealthy men of the capital who loved fine dress buy them up, letting the envoys trade as they wished.

sentences.zh: 使至金玉肆問價，纘曰：「北方金玉大賤，當是山川所出？

translations.literal: When the envoys reached a gold and jade market to ask prices, Zuan said: "Gold and jade are very cheap in the north—surely they come from the mountains and rivers?
translations.idiomatic: When the envoys came to a gold and jade market to ask prices, Zuan said, "Gold and jade are very cheap in the north. Surely they must come from your mountains and rivers?"

sentences.zh: 」安世曰：「聖朝不貴金玉，所以賤同瓦礫。

translations.literal: " Anshi said: "Our sage dynasty does not prize gold and jade, so they are as cheap as tiles and rubble.
translations.idiomatic: " Anshi said, "Our sage dynasty does not prize gold and jade, and so they are valued no higher than tiles and rubble."

sentences.zh: 又皇上德通神明，山不愛寶，故無川無金，無山無玉。

translations.literal: Moreover the Emperor's virtue reaches through to the spirits; the mountains do not hoard their treasures—hence there is no stream without gold, no mountain without jade.
translations.idiomatic: "Moreover the Emperor's virtue reaches to the spirits; the mountains do not hoard their treasures. Thus there is no river without gold and no hill without jade."

sentences.zh: 」纘初將大市，得安世言，慚而罷。

translations.literal: At first Zuan was about to make a large purchase; upon hearing Anshi's words he was ashamed and desisted.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zuan meant to buy heavily, but after hearing Anshi he was ashamed and gave it up.

sentences.zh: 遷主客給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of Guests and Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of Guests and Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 時民困飢流散，豪右多有占奪，安世乃上疏曰：「臣聞量地畫野，經國大式；

translations.literal: At that time the people were distressed by famine and scattered in flight; powerful families often seized land by force. Anshi submitted a memorial saying: "I have heard that measuring land and demarcating the wilds is the great pattern of governing a state;
translations.idiomatic: At that time the people suffered famine and drifted away in flight, and powerful families often seized land by force. Anshi submitted a memorial: "I have heard that measuring land and marking out the realm is the great pattern by which a state is governed;

sentences.zh: 邑地相參，致治之本。

translations.literal: matching settlements to land is the root of achieving good order.
translations.idiomatic: matching settlements to territory is the foundation of good government.

sentences.zh: 井稅之興，其來日久；

translations.literal: The rise of the well-field tax is of long standing;
translations.idiomatic: The well-field tax arose long ago;

sentences.zh: 田萊之數，制之以限。

translations.literal: the number of field and fallow plots was regulated by limits.
translations.idiomatic: and the extent of cultivated and fallow land was fixed by limit.

sentences.zh: 蓋欲使土不曠功，民罔游力。

translations.literal: Surely the intent was to keep the soil from wasting labor and the people from idle strength.
translations.idiomatic: The aim was to keep the soil from lying idle and the people from wasting their strength.

sentences.zh: 雄擅之家，不獨膏腴之美；

translations.literal: Overbearing and monopolizing houses did not alone enjoy the finest fertile soil;
translations.idiomatic: Great predatory houses did not monopolize all the richest land alone;

sentences.zh: 單陋之夫，亦有頃畝之分。

translations.literal: poor and humble men also had their share measured in acres.
translations.idiomatic: poor and humble men also had their measure of acres.

sentences.zh: 所以恤彼貧微，抑茲貪欲，同富約之不均，一齊民於編戶。
