translations.literal: Therefore they comforted the poor and slight, checked such greed, equalized the unevenness of wealth and want, and made the common people one within the registered households.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the poor were sheltered, greed restrained, the imbalance of plenty and want corrected, and the common people brought together as one under the registers.

sentences.zh: 竊見州郡之民，或因年儉流移，棄賣田宅，漂居異鄉，事涉數世。

translations.literal: I have seen that among the people of the provinces and commanderies, because of lean years some drifted away, abandoned and sold fields and houses, drifted to live in other districts, and the matter spanned several generations.
translations.idiomatic: I have observed that in the provinces and commanderies, when years were lean people drifted away, abandoning and selling fields and houses, settling in distant places, until the matter stretched over several generations.

sentences.zh: 三長既立，[8]始返舊墟，廬井荒毀，桑榆改植。

translations.literal: Once the three-chiefs were established, [8] they began to return to old homesteads, but dwellings and wells lay ruined and mulberry and elm had been replanted elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: After the three-chiefs system was established, [8] people began returning to old homesteads, but houses and wells lay in ruins and mulberry and elm trees had been replanted elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 事已歷遠，易生假冒。

translations.literal: The affair had already stretched far in time, and false claims easily arose.
translations.idiomatic: Because so much time had passed, false claims were easily made.

sentences.zh: 強宗豪族，肆其侵凌，遠認魏晉之家，近引親舊之驗。

translations.literal: Powerful clans and great families wantonly encroached, citing distant Wei and Jin households in the far past and near kin and old acquaintances as proof in the recent past.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful clans and great families encroached at will, citing distant Wei and Jin households in the far past and recent kin and old ties as proof.

sentences.zh: 又年載稍久，鄉老所惑，羣證雖多，莫可取據。

translations.literal: Moreover, as the years grew somewhat long, the village elders were confused; though many collective attestations existed, none could be taken as reliable evidence.
translations.idiomatic: As the years lengthened, village elders were bewildered; though witnesses were many, none could serve as reliable proof.

sentences.zh: 各附親知，互有長短，兩證徒具，聽者猶疑，爭訟遷延，連紀不判。

translations.literal: Each side attached itself to kin and acquaintances, mutually contradicting one another; though two sets of testimony were fully presented, the hearers still doubted; lawsuits dragged on, passing years without judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Each party rallied kin and acquaintances, contradicting one another. Two sets of testimony might be complete, yet the judges still hesitated; lawsuits dragged on for years without resolution.

sentences.zh: 良疇委而不開，柔桑枯而不採，僥倖之徒興，繁多之獄作。

translations.literal: Fine fields were left unopened, tender mulberry withered ungathered; opportunists rose up and lawsuits multiplied.
translations.idiomatic: Good fields lay untilled, tender mulberry withered unharvested; opportunists flourished and lawsuits multiplied.

sentences.zh: 欲令家豐歲儲，人給資用，其可得乎！

translations.literal: If one wished to make every household rich in yearly stores and every person supplied with what he needed—how could that be achieved!
translations.idiomatic: If the aim is for every household to store grain and every person to have what he needs, how can that be achieved?

sentences.zh: 愚謂今雖桑井難復，宜更均量，審其徑術，令分藝有準，力業相稱，細民獲資生之利，豪右靡餘地之盈。

translations.literal: I foolishly think that though the mulberry-and-well system is hard to restore, a new equal measure should be made, examining its methods so that division of fields has a standard, labor and occupation match one another, common people gain the profit of livelihood, and powerful families have no surplus land to hoard.
translations.idiomatic: I submit that although the old mulberry-and-well system cannot easily be restored, land should be reassessed and reallocated by clear measure, so that holdings have a standard, labor matches occupation, common people gain a livelihood, and powerful families have no surplus land to hoard.

sentences.zh: 則無私之澤，乃播均於兆庶；

translations.literal: Then the grace without partiality would spread equally among the masses;
translations.idiomatic: Then impartial bounty would reach evenly to the multitude;

sentences.zh: 如阜如山，可有積於比戶矣。

translations.literal: like mounds and mountains, accumulation could exist in every household.
translations.idiomatic: and like hills heaped high, plenty could accumulate in every household.

sentences.zh: 又所爭之田，宜限年斷，事久難明，悉屬今主。

translations.literal: Moreover, disputed fields should be cut off by a limit of years; what is long obscure should all belong to the present holder.
translations.idiomatic: Disputed fields, moreover, should be settled by a time limit: what has long been unclear should belong to the present owner.

sentences.zh: 然後虛妄之民，絕望於覬覦；

translations.literal: Then false and empty people would lose hope of coveting;
translations.idiomatic: Then the false and grasping would lose hope of seizure;

sentences.zh: 守分之士，永免於凌奪矣。

translations.literal: those who kept to their allotted share would forever escape encroachment.
translations.idiomatic: and those who kept to their proper share would forever be safe from seizure."

sentences.zh: 」高祖深納之，後均田之制起於此矣。

translations.literal: " Emperor Gaozu deeply accepted it; afterward the equal-field system arose from this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu accepted this deeply. From this arose the equal-field system.

sentences.zh: 出為安平將軍、相州刺史、假節、趙郡公。

translations.literal: He went out as General of Anping, Governor of Xiang Province, with provisional insignia, Duke of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as General of Anping, Governor of Xiang Province, with provisional insignia, and ennobled Duke of Zhao Commandery.

sentences.zh: 敦勸農桑，禁斷淫祀。

translations.literal: He earnestly encouraged farming and sericulture and forbade illicit sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He earnestly encouraged farming and sericulture and banned improper cults.

sentences.zh: 西門豹、史起，有功於民者，為之修飾廟堂。

translations.literal: For Ximen Bao and Shi Qi, who had merit for the people, he restored and adorned their temple halls.
translations.idiomatic: For Ximen Bao and Shi Qi, who had served the people well, he restored and adorned their temple halls.

sentences.zh: 表薦廣平宋翻、陽平路恃慶，皆為朝廷善士。

translations.literal: He memorialized and recommended Song Fan of Guangping and Lu Shiqing of Yangping, both excellent men of the court.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Song Fan of Guangping and Lu Shiqing of Yangping, both worthy men of the court.

sentences.zh: 初，廣平人李波，宗族強盛，殘掠生民。

translations.literal: At first, Li Bo of Guangping—his clan was powerful and plundered the living people.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, a man of Guangping named Li Bo had a powerful clan that preyed upon the people.

sentences.zh: 前刺史薛道𢷋親往討之，波率其宗族拒戰，大破𢷋軍。

translations.literal: The former governor Xue Daozhen went in person to suppress him; Bo led his clan to resist in battle and thoroughly defeated Daozhen's army.
translations.idiomatic: The previous governor Xue Daozhen went in person to suppress him. Bo rallied his clan to fight and routed Daozhen's army.

sentences.zh: 遂為逋逃之藪，公私成患。

translations.literal: Thereupon it became a lair of fugitives and a trouble to public and private alike.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the place became a refuge for fugitives and a plague to public and private interests alike.

sentences.zh: 百姓為之語曰：「李波小妹字雍容，褰裙逐馬如卷蓬，左射右射必疊雙。

translations.literal: The people made a saying of it: "Li Bo's little sister, styled Yongrong, lifts her skirt and chases horses like rolling tumbleweed; shooting left and right she always hits a pair.
translations.idiomatic: The people had a saying: "Li Bo's little sister, called Yongrong, lifts her skirt and rides after horses like rolling tumbleweed; whether she shoots left or right she always brings down a pair."

sentences.zh: 婦女尚如此，男子那可逢！

translations.literal: If the women are like this, how can one meet the men!
translations.idiomatic: "If the women are like this, what hope have you against the men!"

sentences.zh: 」安世設方略誘波及諸子姪三十餘人，斬于鄴市，境內肅然。

translations.literal: " Anshi devised a stratagem to lure Bo and more than thirty of his sons and nephews, and had them beheaded in the market at Ye; within the jurisdiction all was subdued.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi devised a plan to lure Bo and more than thirty of his sons and nephews, and had them beheaded in the market at Ye. Thereafter the region was quiet.

sentences.zh: 以病免。

translations.literal: Because of illness he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 太和十七年卒于家。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Taihe he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Taihe he died at home.

sentences.zh: 安世妻博陵崔氏，生一子瑒。

translations.literal: Anshi's wife was Lady Cui of Boling; she bore one son, Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi's wife was Lady Cui of Boling, who bore one son, Yang.

sentences.zh: 崔氏以妬悍見出，又尚滄水公主，生二子，謐、郁。

translations.literal: Lady Cui was divorced for jealousy and fierceness; he then married the Princess of Cangshui and had two sons, Mi and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Cui was cast out for jealousy and harsh temper. He then married the Princess of Cangshui and had two sons, Mi and Yu.

sentences.zh: 瑒，字琚羅。

translations.literal: Yang, courtesy name Jurou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang, whose courtesy name was Jurou.

sentences.zh: 涉歷史傳，頗有文才，氣尚豪爽，公強當世。

translations.literal: He ranged through historical records and had considerable literary talent; his spirit was bold and open, and he stood firm and strong in his age.
translations.idiomatic: He read widely in history and had real literary talent. Bold and open in spirit, he stood forthright in his age.

sentences.zh: 延昌末，司徒行參軍，遷司徒長兼主簿。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yanxi era he was Aide in the Department of State Affairs; he was transferred to Senior Clerk and concurrently Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yanxi era he served as Aide in the Department of State Affairs, then was transferred to Senior Clerk and concurrently Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 太師、高陽王雍表薦瑒為其友，正主簿。

translations.literal: The Grand Preceptor, Prince of Gaoyang Yong, memorialized recommending Yang as his companion and made him Chief Clerk in full standing.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Preceptor, Prince of Gaoyang Yong, recommended Yang as his companion and appointed him Chief Clerk in full standing.

sentences.zh: 于時民多絕戶而為沙門，瑒上言：「禮以教世，法導將來，跡用既殊，區流亦別。

translations.literal: At that time many people extinguished their households to become monks. Yang submitted a memorial: "Rites teach the age; law guides what is to come—their traces and uses being different, their spheres and currents are also separate.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many people abandoned their households to become monks. Yang submitted a memorial: "Rites instruct the age and law guides the future. Because their purposes differ, their spheres must be kept apart.

sentences.zh: 故三千之罪，莫大不孝，不孝之大，無過於絕祀。

translations.literal: Therefore among the three thousand offenses none is greater than lack of filial piety; and among the forms of lack of filial piety none exceeds extinguishing the sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Among the three thousand offenses, none is greater than lack of filial piety; and among forms of filial failure, none is worse than cutting off the ancestral sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 然則絕祀之罪，重莫甚焉。

translations.literal: Then the offense of extinguishing the sacrifices—what could be heavier?
translations.idiomatic: The offense of extinguishing the sacrifices, then, could hardly be graver.

sentences.zh: 安得輕縱背禮之情，而肆其向法之意也？

translations.literal: How can one lightly indulge feelings that turn against rites and freely give rein to intentions that turn toward the law?
translations.idiomatic: How then can one lightly indulge feelings that violate ritual and freely indulge intentions that flee into the law?"

sentences.zh: 正使佛道，亦不應然，假令聽然，猶須裁之以禮。

translations.literal: Even if it were the Buddhist Way, it still ought not to be so; even supposing one allowed it, it would still have to be trimmed by rites.
translations.idiomatic: "Even on Buddhist grounds this should not be permitted; even if it were allowed, it would still have to be restrained by ritual.

sentences.zh: 一身親老，棄家絕養，既非人理，尤乖禮情，堙滅大倫，且闕王貫。

translations.literal: When one's own person has aged parents, yet one abandons home and cuts off support—it is already contrary to human reason, especially at odds with ritual feeling; it buries the great human bonds and moreover breaks the king's thread.
translations.idiomatic: To leave aged parents, abandon home, and cut off support is already against human reason and doubly against ritual propriety. It destroys the great human bonds and severs the thread of royal order.

sentences.zh: 交缺當世之禮，而求將來之益，孔子云『未知生，焉知死』，斯言之至，亦為備矣。

translations.literal: One abandons the rites of the present age to seek benefit in the age to come. Confucius said, "If you do not yet know life, how can you know death?"—this saying at its utmost is also complete.
translations.idiomatic: One casts aside the rites of this life to seek profit in the life to come. Confucius said, "If you do not yet understand life, how can you understand death?" That saying, taken to its depth, says all that need be said.

sentences.zh: 安有棄堂堂之政，而從鬼教乎！

translations.literal: How can one abandon the bright governance of the hall and follow the ghost teaching!
translations.idiomatic: How can one abandon the bright governance of the court and follow a ghostly teaching?"

sentences.zh: 又今南服未靜，眾役仍煩，百姓之情，方多避役。

translations.literal: Moreover the south is not yet settled and corvée labor is still heavy; among the common people the tendency to evade service is already strong.
translations.idiomatic: "Moreover the south is not yet pacified and labor service remains heavy. Among the people the urge to evade corvée is already strong.

sentences.zh: 若復聽之，恐捐棄孝慈，比屋而是。

translations.literal: If this were permitted again, I fear filial kindness would be cast aside household after household.
translations.idiomatic: If this were permitted again, I fear filial kindness would be cast aside in household after household."

sentences.zh: 」沙門都統僧暹等忿瑒鬼教之言，以瑒為謗毀佛法，泣訴靈太后，太后責之。

translations.literal: " The Chief of Monks Sengxian and others resented Yang's words about the ghost teaching, taking Yang to be slandering and destroying the Buddhist Law; weeping they appealed to Empress Dowager Ling, and the empress dowager rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief of Monks Sengxian and others, angered by Yang's talk of "ghost teaching," accused him of slandering the Buddhist Law. Weeping, they appealed to Empress Dowager Ling, and the empress dowager rebuked Yang.

sentences.zh: 瑒自理曰：「竊欲清明佛法，使道俗兼通，非敢排棄真學，妄為訾毀。

translations.literal: Yang defended himself: "I wished only to clarify the Buddhist Law and make the way of monks and laymen mutually understood—not daring to reject true learning or recklessly offer slander.
translations.idiomatic: Yang replied in his own defense: "I wished only to clarify the Buddhist Law so that clergy and laity might understand one another. I did not dare reject true learning or recklessly slander it.

sentences.zh: 且鬼神之名，皆通靈達稱，自百代正典，敍三皇五帝，皆號為鬼。

translations.literal: Moreover the names of ghosts and spirits all communicate with the numinous and reach their titles; from the correct classics of a hundred generations, when narrating the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors, all are styled ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the names of ghosts and spirits all refer to beings that reach the numinous realm. From the orthodox classics of a hundred generations, the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors are all called ghosts.

sentences.zh: 天地曰神祇，人死曰鬼。

translations.literal: Heaven and earth are called spirits; when people die they are called ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth are called spirits; the dead are called ghosts.

sentences.zh: 易曰『知鬼神之情狀』，周公自美，亦云『能事鬼神』，禮曰『明則有禮樂，幽則有鬼神』。

translations.literal: The Changes says, "Know the feelings and forms of ghosts and spirits"; Duke of Zhou praised himself and also said, "Able to serve ghosts and spirits"; the Rites say, "What is bright has rites and music; what is dark has ghosts and spirits."
translations.idiomatic: The Changes says, "Know the nature of ghosts and spirits"; the Duke of Zhou praised himself by saying, "Able to serve ghosts and spirits"; the Rites say, "What is bright has rites and music; what is dark has ghosts and spirits."

sentences.zh: 是以明者為堂堂，幽者為鬼教。

translations.literal: Therefore what is bright is called the hall; what is dark is called the ghost teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Thus what is bright is called the hall, and what is dark is called ghost teaching.

sentences.zh: 佛非天非地，本出於人，應世導俗，其道幽隱，名之為鬼，愚謂非謗。

translations.literal: The Buddha is neither heaven nor earth; originally he came forth from man, responding to the age and guiding custom—his way is hidden and obscure, and to name it ghost is, I foolishly think, not slander.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddha is neither heaven nor earth. He arose from mankind, responding to the age and guiding custom. His way is hidden and obscure, and to call it ghost teaching is, I submit, no slander.

sentences.zh: 且心無不善，以佛道為教者，正可未達眾妙之門耳。

translations.literal: Moreover, if the heart is not without goodness, those who take the Buddhist Way as teaching may simply not yet have reached the gate of myriad subtleties.
translations.idiomatic: And if the heart is not without goodness, those who take Buddhism as their teaching may simply not yet have entered the gate of its deepest mysteries."

sentences.zh: 」靈太后雖知瑒言為允，然不免暹等之意，猶罰瑒金一兩。

translations.literal: " Although Empress Dowager Ling knew Yang's words were fair, she could not set aside the feelings of Sengxian and the others; she still fined Yang one liang of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Although Empress Dowager Ling knew Yang's argument was sound, she could not disregard Sengxian and the others; she still fined Yang one liang of gold.

translations.literal: The text is deficient.
translations.idiomatic: The text is deficient.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書郎，加伏波將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Secretariat and given the additional title General Who Calms the Waves.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Secretariat and given the additional title General Who Calms the Waves.

sentences.zh: 隨蕭寶夤西征，以瑒為統軍，假寧遠將軍。

translations.literal: When he followed Xiao Baoyin on the western expedition, Yang was made Commander-in-Chief and given the provisional title General of Pacifying the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: When he followed Xiao Baoyin on the western expedition, Yang was made army commander and given the provisional title General of Pacifying the Distance.

sentences.zh: 瑒德洽鄉閭，招募雄勇，其樂從者數百騎，瑒傾家賑恤，率之西討。

translations.literal: Yang's virtue harmonized with his village and neighborhood; he recruited bold warriors, and several hundred horsemen gladly followed him. Yang spent his family fortune to relieve them and led them west to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Yang was trusted in his home district. He recruited bold warriors, and several hundred horsemen gladly followed. He spent his family fortune to support them and led them west on campaign.

sentences.zh: 寶夤見瑒至，乃拊瑒肩曰：「子遠來，吾事辦矣。

translations.literal: When Baoyin saw Yang arrive, he clapped Yang's shoulder and said: "You have come from afar—my affair is settled.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin saw Yang arrive, he clapped his shoulder and said, "You have come from far away—my task is accomplished."

sentences.zh: 」故其下每有戰功，軍中號曰「李公騎」。

translations.literal: " Therefore whenever his subordinates won merit in battle, the army called them "Lord Li's Horsemen."
translations.idiomatic: After that, whenever his men won distinction in battle, the army called them "Lord Li's Horsemen."

sentences.zh: 寶夤又啟瑒為左丞，仍為別將，軍機戎政，皆與參決。

translations.literal: Baoyin also memorialized to make Yang Left Director and still serve as a separate commander; military plans and frontier administration were all decided with his participation.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin also memorialized to appoint Yang Left Director while keeping him as a separate commander. Military affairs and frontier administration were all decided with his counsel.

sentences.zh: 寶夤又啟為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Baoyin again memorialized to make him Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin again memorialized to appoint him Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 還朝，除鎮遠將軍、岐州刺史，坐辭不赴任免官。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he was appointed General of Pacifying the Distance and Governor of Qi Province; because he declined the appointment he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he was appointed General of Pacifying the Distance and Governor of Qi Province, but because he declined the post he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 建義初，於河陰遇害，時年四十五。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi he was killed at Heyin; he was forty-five.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyi he was killed at Heyin, aged forty-five.

sentences.zh: 初贈鎮東將軍、尚書右僕射、殷州刺史，太昌中重贈散騎常侍、驃騎大將軍、儀同三司、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: At first he was posthumously ennobled General of Pacifying the East, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Governor of Yin Province; in the Taichang era he was again posthumously ennobled Palace Attendant, Grand General of Fast Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, and Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Initially he was posthumously ennobled General of Pacifying the East, Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Governor of Yin Province. In the Taichang era he was again posthumously ennobled Palace Attendant, Grand General of Fast Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, and Governor of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 瑒俶儻有大志，好飲酒，篤於親知，每謂弟郁曰：「士大夫學問，稽博古今而罷，何用專經為老博士也？

translations.literal: Yang was free-spirited and had great ambition; he loved wine and was devoted to kin and friends. He often told his younger brother Yu: "For a gentleman-scholar to study, it is enough to examine broadly the past and present and stop—what use is it to specialize in classics and become an old erudite?
translations.idiomatic: Yang was unconventional and ambitious, fond of wine and deeply loyal to kin and friends. He often told his younger brother Yu, "A gentleman's learning should range broadly through past and present—that is enough. Why bury yourself in the classics and become an old pedant?"

sentences.zh: 」與弟謐特相友愛，謐在鄉物故，瑒慟哭絕氣，久而方蘇，不食數日，期年之中，[10]形骸毀悴。

translations.literal: " With his younger brother Mi he was especially close. When Mi died in the village, Yang wailed until he stopped breathing and only after a long while revived; he ate nothing for several days, and within a year [10] his frame was wasted and haggard.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially close to his younger brother Mi. When Mi died at home, Yang wailed until he stopped breathing and only slowly revived. He ate nothing for days, and within a year [10] he was wasted to skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 人倫哀歎之。

translations.literal: People mourned and sighed over this in human relations.
translations.idiomatic: All who knew them mourned this bond of brotherhood.

sentences.zh: 瑒三子。

translations.literal: Yang had three sons.
translations.idiomatic: Yang had three sons.

sentences.zh: 長子義盛，武定中，司徒倉曹參軍。

translations.literal: The eldest son Yisheng, in the Wuding era, was Aide in the Department of State Affairs' Granary Section.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Yisheng, in the Wuding era, served as Aide in the Granary Section of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 瑒弟謐，字永和。

translations.literal: Yang's younger brother Mi, courtesy name Yonghe.
translations.idiomatic: Yang's younger brother Mi, whose courtesy name was Yonghe.

sentences.zh: 在逸士傳。

translations.literal: He is in the Biographies of Recluses.
translations.idiomatic: His biography appears among the Recluses.

sentences.zh: 謐弟郁，字永穆。

translations.literal: Mi's younger brother Yu, courtesy name Yongmu.
translations.idiomatic: Mi's younger brother Yu, whose courtesy name was Yongmu.

sentences.zh: 好學沉靜，博通經史。

translations.literal: Fond of learning and calm by nature, he was broadly versed in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Fond of learning and calm in temperament, he was broadly versed in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 自著作佐郎為廣平王懷友，懷深相禮遇。

translations.literal: From Associate Author he became companion to Prince Huai of Guangping; Huai treated him with deep courtesy and favor.
translations.idiomatic: From Associate Author he became companion to Prince Huai of Guangping, who treated him with exceptional courtesy.

sentences.zh: 時學士徐遵明教授山東，生徒甚盛，懷徵遵明在館，令郁問其五經義例十餘條，遵明所答數條而已。

translations.literal: At that time the scholar Xu Zunming taught in Shandong and had very many students; Huai summoned Zunming to the mansion and had Yu question him on more than ten items concerning the meaning and examples of the Five Classics; Zunming answered only several items.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the scholar Xu Zunming taught in Shandong and had a great following. Huai summoned Zunming to his residence and had Yu question him on more than ten points of meaning and usage in the Five Classics; Zunming answered only a few.

sentences.zh: 稍遷國子博士。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Erudite of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to Erudite of the National University.

sentences.zh: 自國學之建，諸博士率不講說，朝夕教授，惟郁而已。

translations.literal: From the founding of the National University, the erudites generally did not lecture; morning and evening instruction was given by Yu alone.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of the National University, the erudites generally did not lecture; Yu alone taught morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 謙虛雅寬，甚有儒者之風。

translations.literal: Modest, refined, and generous, he had very much the air of a Confucian.
translations.idiomatic: Modest, refined, and generous, he had the bearing of a true Confucian.

sentences.zh: 遷廷尉少卿，加冠軍將軍，轉通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Justice, given the additional title Champion General, and transferred to Regular Attendant of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Justice with the additional title Champion General, then to Regular Attendant of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 建義中，以兄瑒卒，遂撫育孤姪，歸於鄉里。

translations.literal: During Jianyi, because his elder brother Yang died, he thereupon nurtured the orphaned nephews and returned to his home village.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianyi, after his elder brother Yang died, he raised Yang's orphaned nephews and returned to his home district.

sentences.zh: 永熙初，除散騎常侍、大將軍、[11]左光祿大夫、兼都官尚書，尋領給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi he was appointed Palace Attendant, Grand General, [11] Left Master of Bright Happiness, and concurrently Director of the Ministry of Justice; soon afterward he also held the post of Supervising Secretary of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongxi he was appointed Palace Attendant, Grand General, [11] Left Master of Bright Happiness, and concurrently Director of the Ministry of Justice; soon afterward he also held the post of Supervising Secretary of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 三年春，於顯陽殿講禮，詔郁執經，解說不窮，羣難鋒起，無廢談笑。

translations.literal: In the third year of spring he lectured on rites in the Xianyang Hall; the edict had Yu hold the classics and explain without exhaustion; sharp objections rose in crowds, yet he did not break off his easy conversation.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year he lectured on rites in Xianyang Hall by imperial command. Yu held the classics and explained without end; objections flew thick and fast, yet he never lost his easy composure.

sentences.zh: 出帝及諸王公凡預聽者，莫不嗟善。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor and all the princes and dukes who attended all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The Deposed Emperor and all the princes and dukes present sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 尋病卒，贈散騎常侍、都督定冀相滄殷五州軍事、驃騎大將軍、尚書左僕射、儀同三司、定州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died of illness. Posthumously he was ennobled Palace Attendant, Commander of military affairs in Ding, Ji, Xiang, Cang, and Yin provinces, Grand General of Fast Cavalry, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, and Governor of Ding Province.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he died of illness. Posthumously he was ennobled Palace Attendant, Commander of military affairs in Ding, Ji, Xiang, Cang, and Yin provinces, Grand General of Fast Cavalry, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, and Governor of Ding Province.

sentences.zh: 子士謙，儀同開府參軍事。

translations.literal: His son Shiqian was Aide in an Office Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shiqian served as Aide in an Office Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 李沖，字思順，隴西人，敦煌公寶少子也。

translations.literal: Li Chong, courtesy name Sishun, was a man of Longxi, the youngest son of Duke of Dunhuang Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong, whose courtesy name was Sishun, came from Longxi and was the youngest son of Duke of Dunhuang Bao.

sentences.zh: 少孤，為長兄滎陽太守承所攜訓。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he was taken and instructed by his eldest brother Cheng, Governor of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he was raised and instructed by his eldest brother Cheng, Governor of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 承常言：「此兒器量非恒，方為門戶所寄。

translations.literal: Cheng often said: "This boy's capacity is not ordinary; he will be the one on whom the family line depends.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng often said, "This boy's capacity is extraordinary. The fate of our house will rest on him."

sentences.zh: 」沖沈雅有大量，隨兄至官。

translations.literal: " Chong was deep, refined, and possessed of great breadth; he followed his elder brother to office.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was deep, refined, and magnanimous. He accompanied his elder brother to his post.

sentences.zh: 是時牧守子弟多侵亂民庶，輕有乞奪，沖與承長子韶獨清簡皎然，無所求取，時人美焉。

translations.literal: At that time the sons of governors and prefects often encroached upon and disturbed the common people, lightly begging and seizing; Chong and Cheng's eldest son Shao alone were pure and simple, bright and clear, seeking nothing—at the time people praised them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the sons of governors and prefects often preyed upon the people, taking what they pleased. Chong and Cheng's eldest son Shao alone remained pure and self-restrained, seeking nothing for themselves, and people praised them for it.

sentences.zh: 顯祖末，為中書學生。

translations.literal: At the end of the Xianzu era he was a student of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Xianzu era he was a student of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 沖善交遊，不妄戲雜，流輩重之。

translations.literal: Chong was good at friendship and did not idly mix in frivolous company; his contemporaries respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Chong cultivated friendships wisely and did not idle in frivolous company; his contemporaries respected him.

sentences.zh: 高祖初，以例遷祕書中散，典禁中文事，以修整敏惠，漸見寵待。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Gaozu's reign, by precedent he was transferred to Palace Library Cadet, in charge of confidential documents within the palace; because he was orderly, diligent, and quick-witted, he gradually received favor and trust.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozu's reign he was transferred by precedent to Palace Library Cadet, in charge of confidential palace documents. Orderly, diligent, and quick-witted, he gradually won favor and trust.

sentences.zh: 遷內祕書令、南部給事中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Library Director and Supervising Censor of the Southern Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Library Director and Supervising Censor of the Southern Section.

sentences.zh: 舊無三長，惟立宗主督護，所以民多隱冒，五十、三十家方為一戶。

translations.literal: Formerly there were no three-chiefs; only clan heads and overseers were established, so the people often concealed themselves, and fifty or thirty households formed one registered household.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly there were no three-chiefs; only clan heads and overseers were appointed, so people often hid their numbers and fifty or thirty households were counted as one.

sentences.zh: 沖以三正治民，所由來遠，於是創三長之制而上之。

translations.literal: Chong, because the three chiefs govern the people and the practice is of remote origin, thereupon created the three-chiefs system and submitted it upward.
translations.idiomatic: Chong held that the three-chiefs system for governing the people was ancient in origin, and so devised the three-chiefs system and submitted it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 文明太后覽而稱善，引見公卿議之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wenming read it and praised it, summoning the ministers and dukes to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wenming read it, praised it, and summoned the ministers and dukes to discuss it.

sentences.zh: 中書令鄭羲、祕書令高祐等曰：「沖求立三長者，乃欲混天下一法。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Zheng Xi and Palace Library Director Gao You and others said: "Chong's request to establish three chiefs is meant to unify the realm under one law.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Zheng Xi, Palace Library Director Gao You, and others said, "Chong's proposal to establish three chiefs aims to unify the realm under one law.

sentences.zh: 言似可用，事實難行。

translations.literal: In words it seems usable; in fact it is hard to carry out.
translations.idiomatic: In words it sounds workable; in practice it will be hard to execute."

sentences.zh: 」羲又曰：「不信臣言，但試行之，事敗之後，當知愚言之不謬。

translations.literal: " Xi also said: "If you do not believe my words, just try it. After the affair fails, you will know that my foolish words were not wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Xi also said, "If Your Majesty does not believe me, try it. When it fails, you will see that my warning was not idle."

sentences.zh: 」太尉元丕曰：「臣謂此法若行，於公私有益。

translations.literal: " Grand Commandant Yuan Pi said: "Your subject thinks that if this law is carried out, it will benefit public and private alike.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Yuan Pi said, "I believe that if this law is enacted, it will benefit both public and private interests."

sentences.zh: 」咸稱方今有事之月，校比民戶，新舊未分，民必勞怨，請過今秋，至冬閑月，徐乃遣使，於事為宜，沖曰：「民者，冥也，可使由之，不可使知之。

translations.literal: " All said that in the present month of pressing affairs, comparing and checking households, with old and new not yet divided, the people would surely labor and resent it; they asked to pass this autumn and wait until the winter slack month, then slowly dispatch envoys—that would be suitable for the affair. Chong said: "The people are dark; they may be made to follow, but not made to understand.
translations.idiomatic: All agreed that in the present busy season, with household registers still being checked and old and new not yet sorted, the people would surely resent the burden. They asked to wait until autumn had passed and dispatch envoys in the winter slack season. Chong said, "The people are simple: they may be led to act, but they must not be made to understand beforehand.

sentences.zh: 若不因調時，百姓徒知立長校戶之勤，未見均徭省賦之益，心必生怨。

translations.literal: If it is not done at the time of tax collection, the common people will only know the labor of establishing chiefs and checking households and will not see the benefit of equal corvée and reduced levies—their hearts will surely breed resentment.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not act during the tax season, the people will know only the labor of appointing chiefs and checking households, and not yet see the benefit of equal corvée and lighter levies. Resentment will surely follow.

sentences.zh: 宜及課調之月，令知賦稅之均。

translations.literal: It is fitting to do it in the month of tax collection and assessment, and let them know that levies are equal.
translations.idiomatic: We should act during the tax-assessment month and let them see that the burdens are equal.

sentences.zh: 既識其事，又得其利，因民之欲，為之易行。

translations.literal: Once they know the affair and also obtain its profit, by the people's desire it will be easy to carry out.
translations.idiomatic: Once they understand the matter and feel the benefit, the reform will follow their own desire and be easy to enact."

sentences.zh: 」著作郎傅思益進曰：「民俗既異，險易不同，九品差調，為日已久，一旦改法，恐成擾亂。

translations.literal: " Author Gentleman Fu Siyi advanced and said: "Customs already differ; ruggedness and ease are not the same; the nine ranks of differential adjustment have long been in place—suddenly to change the law, I fear it will become disturbance and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Author Gentleman Fu Siyi stepped forward and said, "Customs already differ and terrain varies. The nine-rank system of differential taxation has long stood. To change the law at once may cause turmoil."

sentences.zh: 」太后曰：「立三長，則課有常準，賦有恒分，苞蔭之戶可出，僥倖之人可止，何為而不可？

translations.literal: " The empress dowager said: "If three chiefs are established, then tax assessment will have a constant standard and levies a fixed share; sheltered households can be brought out and opportunists can be stopped—why should it not be done?
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager said, "If three chiefs are established, tax assessment will have a fixed standard and levies a constant share. Hidden households can be exposed and opportunists checked. Why should it not be done?"

sentences.zh: 」羣議雖有乖異，然惟以變法為難，更無異義。

translations.literal: " Though the assembled discussion had divergences, yet only change of law was difficult; there was no other dissent.
translations.idiomatic: Though the assembly differed, their objection was only that reform would be difficult; there was no other fundamental dissent.

sentences.zh: 遂立三長，公私便之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the three chiefs were established, and public and private alike found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The three-chiefs system was then established, to the benefit of public and private alike.

sentences.zh: 遷中書令，加散騎常侍，給事中如故。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Secretariat, given the additional title Palace Attendant, and remained Supervising Censor as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Director of the Secretariat with the additional title Palace Attendant, retaining his post as Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 尋轉南部尚書，賜爵順陽侯。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to Director of the Southern Section and ennobled Marquis of Shunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to Director of the Southern Section and ennobled Marquis of Shunyang.

sentences.zh: 沖為文明太后所幸，恩寵日盛，賞賜月至數千萬，進爵隴西公，密致珍寶御物以充其第，外人莫得而知焉。

translations.literal: Chong was favored by Empress Dowager Wenming; his grace and favor grew daily, and rewards reached several tens of millions each month. He was advanced to Duke of Longxi; rare treasures and imperial goods were secretly sent to fill his residence— outsiders could not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: Chong won the favor of Empress Dowager Wenming. Honors and gifts mounted month by month until they reached tens of millions. He was advanced to Duke of Longxi, and rare treasures and imperial goods were secretly sent to fill his house—unknown to outsiders.

sentences.zh: 沖家素清貧，於是始為富室。

translations.literal: Chong's family had always been poor; from this he became a wealthy house.
translations.idiomatic: The Li family had always been poor; now for the first time they became rich.

sentences.zh: 而謙以自牧，積而能散，近自姻族，逮于鄉閭，莫不分及。

translations.literal: Yet he was humble in self-restraint, accumulating yet able to disperse; from near kin to village and neighborhood, none was left without a share.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he remained humble and self-restrained, gathering wealth only to give it away. From close kin to neighbors, none was left without a share.

sentences.zh: 虛己接物，垂念羇寒，衰舊淪屈由之躋敍者，亦以多矣。

translations.literal: Emptying himself in dealing with others, caring for the estranged and cold, many who had sunk in decline and obscurity rose through the ranks because of him.
translations.idiomatic: He humbled himself in all his dealings, looked after the displaced and the poor, and many who had fallen into obscurity and neglect were raised through his patronage.

sentences.zh: 時以此稱之。

translations.literal: At the time he was praised for this.
translations.idiomatic: At the time he was widely praised for this.

sentences.zh: 初，沖兄佐與河南太守來崇同自涼州入國，素有微嫌。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chong's elder brother Zuo and Lai Chong, Administrator of Henan, had together entered the realm from Liangzhou; they had long harbored slight animosity.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Chong's elder brother Zuo and Lai Chong, Administrator of Henan, had entered the realm together from Liangzhou; they had long nursed a slight grudge between them.

sentences.zh: 佐因緣成崇罪，餓死獄中。

translations.literal: Zuo seized an opportunity to fabricate Lai Chong's guilt; Lai Chong starved to death in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo seized an opportunity to frame Lai Chong on false charges, and Lai Chong starved to death in prison.

sentences.zh: 後崇子護又糾佐贓罪，佐及沖等悉坐幽繫，會赦乃免，佐甚銜之。

translations.literal: Later Lai Chong's son Hu denounced Zuo for corruption; Zuo, Chong, and the others were all imprisoned, but were released when an amnesty was proclaimed. Zuo deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lai Chong's son Hu denounced Zuo for corruption. Zuo, Chong, and the others were all imprisoned and were released only when an amnesty was proclaimed. Zuo deeply resented it.

sentences.zh: 至沖寵貴，綜攝內外，護為南部郎，深慮為沖所陷，常求退避，而沖每慰撫之。

translations.literal: When Chong rose to favor and high rank and held comprehensive authority within and without, Hu served as a secretary in the Southern Bureau. He greatly feared being trapped by Chong and constantly sought to withdraw, but Chong always reassured and comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong rose to favor and high office and held comprehensive authority at court and beyond, Hu served as a secretary in the Southern Bureau. He greatly feared being ensnared by Chong and constantly sought to withdraw, but Chong always reassured and comforted him.

sentences.zh: 護後坐贓罪，懼必不濟。

translations.literal: Hu was later implicated in a corruption offense and feared he would not escape punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Hu was later implicated in a corruption case and feared he would not escape punishment.

sentences.zh: 沖乃具奏與護本末嫌隙，乞原恕之，遂得不坐。

translations.literal: Chong then submitted a full memorial detailing his entire history of grievance with Hu and begged that he be pardoned; Hu thus escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Chong then submitted a full memorial recounting his entire history of grievance with Hu and begged that he be pardoned. Hu thus escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 沖從甥陰始孫孤貧，往來沖家，至如子姪。

translations.literal: Chong's maternal nephew Yin Shisun was orphaned and poor; he came and went at Chong's household as intimately as sons and nephews.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's maternal nephew Yin Shisun was orphaned and poor. He came and went at Chong's household as freely as sons and nephews.

sentences.zh: 有人求官，因其納馬於沖，始孫受輒而不為言。

translations.literal: Someone seeking an office presented a horse to Chong through him; Shisun accepted it but said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Someone seeking an appointment presented a horse to Chong through him. Shisun accepted it but said nothing.

sentences.zh: 後假方便，借沖此馬，馬主見沖乘馬而不得官，後乃自陳始末。

translations.literal: Later, taking advantage of an opportunity, he borrowed this horse from Chong. The owner of the horse saw Chong riding it yet failed to obtain an office, and afterward stated the whole affair himself.
translations.idiomatic: Later, taking advantage of an opportunity, he borrowed the horse from Chong. The owner saw Chong riding it yet failed to obtain an appointment, and afterward reported the whole affair himself.

sentences.zh: 沖聞之，大驚，執始孫以狀款奏，始孫坐死。

translations.literal: When Chong heard of it he was greatly alarmed. He seized Shisun and submitted a truthful report; Shisun was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong heard of it he was greatly alarmed. He seized Shisun and submitted a truthful report, and Shisun was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 其處要自厲，不念愛惡，皆此類也。

translations.literal: In handling important matters he disciplined himself strictly, setting aside personal affection and dislike — all his conduct was of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: In handling important affairs he held himself to strict standards, setting aside personal likes and dislikes. All his conduct was of this kind.

sentences.zh: 是時循舊，王公重臣皆呼其名，高祖常謂沖為中書而不名之。

translations.literal: At that time, following custom, princes, dukes, and high ministers were all addressed by their personal names. The Emperor always called Chong "Director of the Palace Secretariat" rather than naming him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, following custom, princes, dukes, and high ministers were all addressed by their personal names. The Emperor always called Chong "Director of the Palace Secretariat" rather than use his name.

sentences.zh: 文明太后崩後，高祖居喪，引見待接有加。

translations.literal: After Empress Dowager Wenming passed away, the Emperor observed mourning. When he received audiences, his treatment of Chong was especially generous.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Dowager Wenming died, the Emperor observed mourning. In audiences his treatment of Chong was especially generous.

sentences.zh: 及議禮儀律令，潤飾辭旨，刊定輕重，高祖雖自下筆，無不訪決焉。

translations.literal: When ritual, law, and statutes were debated, he polished the wording and fixed penalties and mitigations. Though the Emperor himself wrote, he always consulted Chong before deciding.
translations.idiomatic: When ritual, law, and statutes were debated, he polished the wording and fixed penalties and mitigations. Though the Emperor drafted the texts himself, he always consulted Chong before deciding.

sentences.zh: 沖竭忠奉上，知無不盡，出入憂勤，形於顏色，雖舊臣戚輔，莫能逮之，無不服其明斷慎密而歸心焉。

translations.literal: Chong devoted himself utterly in service to the throne, withholding nothing he knew. His constant care and exertion showed in his countenance. Even old ministers and kinsmen among the chief counselors could not match him; none failed to admire his clarity of judgment and careful discretion, and all gave him their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Chong served the throne with complete loyalty, withholding nothing he knew. His constant care and exertion showed in his face. Even old ministers and kinsmen among the chief counselors could not match him. All admired his clarity of judgment and careful discretion, and gave him their hearts.

sentences.zh: 於是天下翕然，及殊方聽望，咸宗奇之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the realm fell into harmonious accord, and even those in distant regions who heard of him and looked his way all regarded him with admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the realm fell into harmony, and even those in distant regions who heard of him and looked his way regarded him with admiration.

sentences.zh: 高祖亦深相杖信，親敬彌甚，君臣之間，情義莫二。

translations.literal: The Emperor also relied on and trusted him deeply, treating him with ever greater personal regard. Between ruler and minister, their bond of loyalty and affection knew no second.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor also relied on and trusted him deeply, treating him with ever greater personal regard. Between ruler and minister their bond of loyalty and affection was singular.

sentences.zh: 及改置百司，開建五等，以沖參定典式，封滎陽郡開國侯，食邑八百戶，拜廷尉卿。

translations.literal: When the hundred offices were reorganized and the five ranks of nobility established, Chong was appointed to help set the canonical forms. He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xingyang Commandery with a fief of eight hundred households and appointed Director of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When the hundred offices were reorganized and the five ranks of nobility established, Chong was appointed to help set the canonical forms. He was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xingyang Commandery with a fief of eight hundred households and appointed Director of the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 尋遷侍中、吏部尚書、咸陽王師。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Palace Attendant, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and Preceptor to the Prince of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Palace Attendant, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and Preceptor to the Prince of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 東宮既建，拜太子少傅。

translations.literal: Once the Eastern Palace was established, he was appointed Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Eastern Palace was established, he was appointed Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 高祖初依周禮，置夫、嬪之列，以沖女為夫人。

translations.literal: When the Emperor first followed the Rites of Zhou in establishing the ranks of lady and consort, he made Chong's daughter a Lady.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor first followed the Rites of Zhou in establishing the ranks of lady and consort, he made Chong's daughter a Lady.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「昔軒皇誕御，垂棟宇之構；

translations.literal: Edict: "In antiquity the Yellow Emperor ascended the throne and bequeathed the plan of halls and roofs;
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "In antiquity the Yellow Emperor ascended the throne and bequeathed the plan of halls and roofs;

sentences.zh: 爰歷三代，興宮觀之式。

translations.literal: through the Three Dynasties the model of palaces and towers was raised.
translations.idiomatic: through the Three Dynasties the model of palaces and towers was raised.

sentences.zh: 然茅茨土堦，昭德於上代；

translations.literal: Yet thatched roofs and earthen steps displayed virtue in earlier ages;
translations.idiomatic: Yet thatched roofs and earthen steps displayed virtue in earlier ages;

sentences.zh: 層臺廣厦，崇威於中葉。

translations.literal: while tiered terraces and broad halls elevated majesty in the middle age.
translations.idiomatic: while tiered terraces and broad halls elevated majesty in the middle age.

sentences.zh: 良由文質異宜，華樸殊禮故也。

translations.literal: This was truly because ornament and substance suited different times, and splendor and simplicity followed different rites.
translations.idiomatic: This was because ornament and substance suited different times, and splendor and simplicity followed different rites.

sentences.zh: 是以周成繼業，營明堂於東都；

translations.literal: Therefore King Cheng of Zhou, succeeding to the enterprise, built the Bright Hall in the eastern capital;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore King Cheng of Zhou, succeeding to the enterprise, built the Bright Hall in the eastern capital;

sentences.zh: 漢祖聿興，建未央於咸鎬。

translations.literal: and the Founding Emperor of Han, rising swiftly, raised Weiyang Palace at Xian and Hao.
translations.idiomatic: and the Founding Emperor of Han, rising swiftly, raised Weiyang Palace at Xian and Hao.

sentences.zh: 蓋所以尊嚴皇威，崇重帝德，豈好奢惡儉，苟弊民力者哉？

translations.literal: Surely this was to dignify imperial majesty and exalt the Emperor's virtue — not from love of extravagance or hatred of thrift, nor from casually exhausting the people's strength?
translations.idiomatic: Surely this was to dignify imperial majesty and exalt the Emperor's virtue — not from love of extravagance or hatred of thrift, nor from casually exhausting the people's strength?

sentences.zh: 我皇運統天，協纂乾曆，銳意四方，未遑建制，宮室之度，頗為未允。

translations.literal: Our August House, its destiny aligned with Heaven, jointly inherited the mandate of Qian. Intent on the four quarters, we had no leisure to establish institutions; the scale of palace halls has fallen somewhat short of what is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty, its destiny aligned with Heaven, jointly inherited the mandate. Intent on the four quarters, we had no leisure to establish institutions, and the scale of palace halls has fallen somewhat short of what is fitting.

sentences.zh: 太祖初基，雖粗有經式，自茲厥後，復多營改。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor first laid the foundation, there was a rough standard; since then there have been many revisions and rebuildings.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Ancestor first laid the foundation, there was a rough standard; since then there have been many revisions and rebuildings.

sentences.zh: 至於三元慶饗，萬國充庭，觀光之使，具瞻有闕。

translations.literal: When the Three First Days are celebrated and the myriad states fill the court, emissaries come to behold our splendor — yet what meets the eye falls short.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three First Days are celebrated and the myriad states fill the court, emissaries come to behold our splendor — yet what meets the eye falls short.

sentences.zh: 朕以寡德，猥承洪緒，運屬休期，事鍾昌運，宜遵遠度，式茲宮宇。

translations.literal: I, of slender virtue, have unworthily received the great succession. Our fortune falls in an age of prosperity; affairs coincide with a season of flourishing. We ought to follow distant precedents and thereby give form to these palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: I, of slender virtue, have unworthily received the great succession. Our fortune falls in an age of prosperity; affairs coincide with a season of flourishing. We ought to follow distant precedents and thereby give form to these palace halls.

sentences.zh: 指訓規模，事昭於平日；

translations.literal: Plans and measures have been set forth and made plain in ordinary days;
translations.idiomatic: Plans and measures have been set forth and made plain in ordinary days;

sentences.zh: 明堂、太廟，已成於昔年。

translations.literal: the Bright Hall and Grand Ancestral Temple were completed in years past.
translations.idiomatic: the Bright Hall and Grand Ancestral Temple were completed in years past.

sentences.zh: 又因往歲之豐資，藉民情之安逸，將以今春營改正殿。

translations.literal: Taking also last year's abundant resources and the people's ease of mind, we intend this spring to build and rectify the main hall.
translations.idiomatic: Taking also last year's abundant resources and the people's ease of mind, we intend this spring to build and rectify the main hall.

sentences.zh: 違犯時令，行之惕然。

translations.literal: To violate the seasons in doing so makes one proceed with trepidation.
translations.idiomatic: To violate the seasons in doing so makes one proceed with trepidation.

sentences.zh: 但朔土多寒，事殊南夏，自非裁度當春，興役徂暑，則廣制崇基，莫由克就。

translations.literal: But the northern lands are largely cold, unlike the south; unless planning begins in spring and labor proceeds through summer, there is no way to complete so broad a foundation and so lofty a base.
translations.idiomatic: But the northern lands are largely cold, unlike the south. Unless planning begins in spring and labor proceeds through summer, there is no way to complete so broad a foundation and so lofty a base.

sentences.zh: 成功立事，非委賢莫可；

translations.literal: To succeed in an enterprise, nothing avails without entrusting it to the worthy;
translations.idiomatic: To succeed in an enterprise, nothing avails without entrusting it to the worthy;

sentences.zh: 改制規模，非任能莫濟。

translations.literal: to reform the design, nothing succeeds without assigning the capable.
translations.idiomatic: to reform the design, nothing succeeds without assigning the capable.

sentences.zh: 尚書沖器懷淵博，經度明遠，可領將作大匠；

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Chong is broad of capacity and profound of mind, clear and far-seeing in planning — let him take charge as Master of Works;
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Chong is broad of capacity and profound of mind, clear and far-seeing in planning — let him take charge as Master of Works;

sentences.zh: 司空、長樂公亮，可與大匠共監興繕。

translations.literal: the Director of Works, Duke of Changle Liang, may jointly oversee the construction with the Master of Works.
translations.idiomatic: the Director of Works, Duke of Changle Liang, may jointly oversee the construction with the Master of Works.

sentences.zh: 其去故崇新之宜，修復太極之制，朕當別加指授。」

translations.literal: As for what is fit in removing the old and elevating the new, and restoring the form of the Grand Ultimate Hall, We shall issue separate instructions."
translations.idiomatic: As for what is fit in removing the old and elevating the new, and restoring the form of the Grand Ultimate Hall, We shall issue separate instructions."

sentences.zh: 車駕南伐，加沖輔國大將軍，統眾翼從。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage marched south on campaign, Chong was made General-in-Chief of State Support and commanded the host in flank escort.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage marched south on campaign, Chong was made General-in-Chief of State Support and commanded the host in flank escort.

sentences.zh: 自發都至於洛陽，霖雨不霽，仍詔六軍發軫。

translations.literal: From the departure from the capital until Luoyang, unceasing downpours persisted, yet an edict still ordered the six armies to set out.
translations.idiomatic: From the departure from the capital until Luoyang, unceasing downpours persisted, yet an edict still ordered the six armies to set out.

sentences.zh: 高祖戎服執鞭，御馬而出，羣臣啟顙於馬首之前。

translations.literal: The Emperor, in martial dress, took the whip and rode forth. The officials bowed their foreheads before his horse's head.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, in martial dress, took the whip and rode forth. The officials bowed their foreheads before his horse's head.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「長驅之謀，廟算已定，今大軍將進，公等更欲何云？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The plan for a long advance and the calculations in the ancestral temple are already settled. Now the great army is about to march — what more do you wish to say?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "The plan for a long advance and the calculations in the ancestral temple are already settled. Now the great army is about to march — what more do you wish to say?

sentences.zh: 」沖進曰：「臣等不能折衝帷幄，坐制四海，而令南有竊號之渠，實臣等之咎。

translations.literal: "Chong stepped forward and said: "We your ministers have been unable to break the enemy within the command tent and govern the four seas from our seats, yet south of us a usurper holds a stolen title — truly this is our fault.
translations.idiomatic: "Chong stepped forward and said: "We your ministers have been unable to break the enemy within the command tent and govern the four seas from our seats, yet south of us a usurper holds a stolen title — truly this is our fault.

sentences.zh: 陛下以文軌未一，親勞聖駕，臣等誠思亡軀盡命，効死戎行。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, because the civil order and imperial roads are not yet unified, personally labors with the sacred carriage. We truly wish to exhaust our bodies and spend our lives, dying in the field of battle.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, because the civil order and imperial roads are not yet unified, personally labors with the sacred carriage. We truly wish to exhaust our bodies and spend our lives, dying in the field of battle.

sentences.zh: 然自離都淫雨，士馬困弊，前路尚遙，水潦方甚。

translations.literal: Yet since leaving the capital there has been incessant rain; men and horses are weary and depleted. The road ahead is still far, and the floods are now severe.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since leaving the capital there has been incessant rain; men and horses are weary and depleted. The road ahead is still far, and the floods are now severe.

sentences.zh: 且伊洛境內，小水猶尚致難，況長江浩汗，越在南境。

translations.literal: Moreover, within the Yi and Luo region even small streams still cause trouble — how much more the vast Yangzi River, which lies beyond our southern frontier?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, within the Yi and Luo region even small streams still cause trouble — how much more the vast Yangzi River, which lies beyond our southern frontier?

sentences.zh: 若營舟檝，必須停滯，師老糧乏，進退為難，矜喪反旆，於義為允。

translations.literal: If we must build boats and oars, we shall have to halt. The army will age, provisions will run short, advance and retreat will both be difficult. To show pity in mourning and turn the banners homeward would be right by principle.
translations.idiomatic: If we must build boats and oars, we shall have to halt. The army will age, provisions will run short, advance and retreat will both be difficult. To show pity in mourning and turn the banners homeward would be right by principle.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「一同之意，前已具論。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The wish for unification — I have already stated it fully before.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "The wish for unification — I have already stated it fully before.

sentences.zh: 卿等正以水雨為難，然天時頗亦可知。

translations.literal: You take the rain as the difficulty, yet the seasons are in some measure knowable.
translations.idiomatic: You take the rain as the difficulty, yet the seasons are in some measure knowable.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: How so?
translations.idiomatic: How so?

sentences.zh: 夏既炎旱，秋故雨多，玄冬之初，必當開爽。

translations.literal: Summer having been scorching and dry, autumn therefore brings much rain. At the start of deep winter, the skies will surely clear.
translations.idiomatic: Summer having been scorching and dry, autumn therefore brings much rain. At the start of deep winter, the skies will surely clear.

sentences.zh: 比後月十間，[12]若雨猶不已，此乃天也，脫於此而晴，行則無害。

translations.literal: Within the next ten days or so,[12] if rain still does not cease, that will be Heaven's doing; but if the skies clear by then, marching will do no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Within the next ten days or so,[12] if rain still does not cease, that will be Heaven's doing; but if the skies clear by then, marching will do no harm.

sentences.zh: 古不伐喪，謂諸侯同軌之國，非王者統一之文。

translations.literal: In antiquity "do not campaign against a state in mourning" referred to feudal lords of the same roads — not to the king's text of unification.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity "do not campaign against a state in mourning" referred to feudal lords of the same roads — not to the king's text of unification.

sentences.zh: 已至於此，何容停駕。

translations.literal: Having come this far, how can we halt the carriage?
translations.idiomatic: Having come this far, how can we halt the carriage?

sentences.zh: 」沖又進曰：「今者之舉，天下所不願，唯陛下欲之。

translations.literal: "Chong stepped forward again: "This present undertaking is what the realm does not wish for — only Your Majesty desires it.
translations.idiomatic: "Chong stepped forward again: "This present undertaking is what the realm does not wish for — only Your Majesty desires it.

sentences.zh: 漢文言，吾獨乘千里馬，竟何至也？

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han said, "Shall I alone ride a thousand-li horse — where would that lead?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han said, "Shall I alone ride a thousand-li horse — where would that lead?"

sentences.zh: 臣有意而無其辭，敢以死請。

translations.literal: I have the intent but not the words; I dare beg with my life.
translations.idiomatic: I have the intent but not the words; I dare beg with my life.

sentences.zh: 」高祖大怒曰：「方欲經營宇宙，一同區域，而卿等儒生，屢疑大計，斧鉞有常，卿勿復言！

translations.literal: The Emperor said in great anger: "I am just setting out to order the universe and unify the realm, yet you Confucian scholars repeatedly doubt the great plan. The axe and punishment stand ready — speak no more!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said in great anger: "I am just setting out to order the universe and unify the realm, yet you Confucian scholars repeatedly doubt the great plan. The axe and punishment stand ready — speak no more!

sentences.zh: 」策馬將出。

translations.literal: "He spurred his horse and was about to depart.
translations.idiomatic: "He spurred his horse and was about to depart.

sentences.zh: 於是大司馬、安定王休，兼左僕射、任城王澄等並殷勤泣諫。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Grand Marshal, Prince of Anding Xiu, and the Concurrent Left Deputy Director, Prince of Rencheng Cheng, among others, all earnestly remonstrated with tears.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Grand Marshal, Prince of Anding Xiu, and the Concurrent Left Deputy Director, Prince of Rencheng Cheng, among others, all earnestly remonstrated with tears.

sentences.zh: 高祖乃諭羣臣曰：「今者興動不小，動而無成，何以示後？

translations.literal: The Emperor then addressed the officials: "This undertaking is no small matter. If we move and achieve nothing, how shall we show posterity?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then addressed the officials: "This undertaking is no small matter. If we move and achieve nothing, how shall we show posterity?

sentences.zh: 苟欲班師，無以垂之千載。

translations.literal: If we wish to withdraw the army, there is nothing to hand down through a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: If we wish to withdraw the army, there is nothing to hand down through a thousand years.

sentences.zh: 朕仰惟遠祖，世居幽漠，違眾南遷，以享無窮之美，豈其無心，輕遺陵壤。

translations.literal: Reflecting on our distant ancestors who dwelt in the wild north, they went against the multitude and migrated south to enjoy boundless blessings — was it that they had no heart for the old tombs and lightly abandoned their ancestral land?
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on our distant ancestors who dwelt in the wild north, they went against the multitude and migrated south to enjoy boundless blessings — was it that they had no heart for the old tombs and lightly abandoned their ancestral land?

sentences.zh: 今之君子，寧獨有懷？

translations.literal: Do gentlemen today alone cherish such thoughts?
translations.idiomatic: Do gentlemen today alone cherish such thoughts?

sentences.zh: 當由天工人代、王業須成故也。

translations.literal: Surely it is because Heaven entrusts work to men and the royal enterprise must be completed.
translations.idiomatic: Surely it is because Heaven entrusts work to men and the royal enterprise must be completed.

sentences.zh: 若不南鑾，即當移都於此，光宅土中，機亦時矣，王公等以為何如？

translations.literal: If we do not march south, then we must move the capital here, making our luminous abode in the Middle Land — the moment is timely. Princes and dukes, what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: If we do not march south, then we must move the capital here, making our luminous abode in the Middle Land — the moment is timely. Princes and dukes, what do you think?

sentences.zh: 議之所決，不得旋踵，欲遷者左，不欲者右。

translations.literal: The decision of this deliberation brooks no delay: those who wish to move, to the left; those who do not, to the right.
translations.idiomatic: The decision of this deliberation brooks no delay: those who wish to move, to the left; those who do not, to the right.

sentences.zh: 」安定王休等相率如右。

translations.literal: "Prince of Anding Xiu and the others in succession went to the right.
translations.idiomatic: "Prince of Anding Xiu and the others in succession went to the right.

sentences.zh: 前南安王楨進曰：[13]「夫愚者闇於成事，智者見於未萌。

translations.literal: Former Prince of Nan'an Zhen stepped forward:[13] "The foolish are blind to completed affairs; the wise see what has not yet sprouted.
translations.idiomatic: Former Prince of Nan'an Zhen stepped forward:[13] "The foolish are blind to completed affairs; the wise see what has not yet sprouted.

sentences.zh: 行至德者不議於俗，成大功者不謀於眾，非常之人乃能建非常之事。

translations.literal: One who walks in supreme virtue does not debate with the vulgar; one who completes a great achievement does not consult the multitude. Only an extraordinary man can accomplish an extraordinary deed.
translations.idiomatic: One who walks in supreme virtue does not debate with the vulgar; one who completes a great achievement does not consult the multitude. Only an extraordinary man can accomplish an extraordinary deed.

sentences.zh: [14]廓神都以延王業，度土中以制帝京，周公啟之於前，陛下行之於後，故其宜也。

translations.literal: [14]To broaden the divine capital and extend the royal enterprise, to measure the Middle Land and establish the imperial seat — the Duke of Zhou opened the way before, Your Majesty walks it after; therefore it is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: [14]To broaden the divine capital and extend the royal enterprise, to measure the Middle Land and establish the imperial seat — the Duke of Zhou opened the way before, Your Majesty walks it after; therefore it is fitting.

sentences.zh: 且天下至重，莫若皇居，人之所貴，寧如遺體？

translations.literal: Moreover, nothing under Heaven is weightier than the imperial residence; what men hold dear — is it not like their own bodies left behind?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, nothing under Heaven is weightier than the imperial residence; what men hold dear — is it not like their own bodies left behind?

sentences.zh: 請上安聖躬，下慰民望，光宅中原，輟彼南伐。

translations.literal: We beg that above, the sacred person be secured; below, the people's hopes be soothed; that the luminous abode be in the Central Plain, and the southern campaign be set aside.
translations.idiomatic: We beg that above, the sacred person be secured; below, the people's hopes be soothed; that the luminous abode be in the Central Plain, and the southern campaign be set aside.

sentences.zh: 此臣等願言，蒼生幸甚。

translations.literal: This is what we your ministers wish to say — the common people would be greatly blessed.
translations.idiomatic: This is what we your ministers wish to say — the common people would be greatly blessed.

sentences.zh: 」羣臣咸唱「萬歲」。

translations.literal: "The officials all cried "Long may he live ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: "The officials all cried "Long may he live ten thousand years!"

sentences.zh: 高祖初謀南遷，恐眾心戀舊，乃示為大舉，因以脅定羣情，外名南伐，其實遷也。

translations.literal: When the Emperor first planned the southern move of the capital, fearing that minds would cling to the old seat, he displayed a great campaign in order to coerce and fix the officials' minds — outwardly named a southern expedition, in truth a relocation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor first planned the southern move of the capital, fearing that minds would cling to the old seat, he displayed a great campaign in order to coerce and fix the officials' minds — outwardly named a southern expedition, in truth a relocation.

sentences.zh: 舊人懷土，多所不願，內憚南征，無敢言者，於是定都洛陽。

translations.literal: The old families, attached to their land, largely did not wish it; inwardly they feared the southern campaign but none dared speak. Thereupon the capital was fixed at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The old families, attached to their land, largely did not wish it; inwardly they feared the southern campaign but none dared speak. Thereupon the capital was fixed at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 沖言於高祖曰：「陛下方修周公之制，定鼎成周。

translations.literal: Chong said to the Emperor: "Your Majesty is just now enacting the Duke of Zhou's institutions and fixing the sacred tripod at Chengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chong said to the Emperor: "Your Majesty is just now enacting the Duke of Zhou's institutions and fixing the sacred tripod at Chengzhou.

sentences.zh: 然營建六寢，不可遊駕待就；

translations.literal: Yet the six palaces cannot be built while the imperial carriage waits idle;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the six palaces cannot be built while the imperial carriage waits idle;

sentences.zh: 興築城郛，難以馬上營訖。

translations.literal: raising walls and ramparts cannot be finished from horseback.
translations.idiomatic: raising walls and ramparts cannot be finished from horseback.

sentences.zh: 願暫還北都，令臣下經造，功成事訖，然後備文物之章，和玉鑾之響，巡時南徙，軌儀土中。

translations.literal: We beg to return temporarily to the northern capital, let your ministers carry out the construction, and when the work is complete and affairs settled, then array the insignia of civilization, harmonize the jade bells of the imperial carriage, and at the proper season move south to take up the ceremonial standards in the Middle Land.
translations.idiomatic: We beg to return temporarily to the northern capital, let your ministers carry out the construction, and when the work is complete and affairs settled, then array the insignia of civilization, harmonize the jade bells of the imperial carriage, and at the proper season move south to take up the ceremonial standards in the Middle Land.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「朕將巡省方岳，至鄴小停，春始便還，未宜遂不歸北。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I shall tour and inspect the sacred mountains. I shall stop briefly at Ye; at the start of spring I shall return — it is not yet fitting to resolve never to go back north.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "I shall tour and inspect the sacred mountains. I shall stop briefly at Ye; at the start of spring I shall return — it is not yet fitting to resolve never to go back north.

sentences.zh: 」尋以沖為鎮南將軍，侍中、少傅如故，委以營構之任。

translations.literal: "Soon thereafter Chong was made General Who Guards the South; his posts as Palace Attendant and Junior Tutor remained as before, and he was entrusted with the task of construction.
translations.idiomatic: "Soon thereafter Chong was made General Who Guards the South; his posts as Palace Attendant and Junior Tutor remained as before, and he was entrusted with the task of construction.

sentences.zh: 改封陽平郡開國侯，邑戶如先。

translations.literal: His enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Yangping Commandery with a fief of households as before.
translations.idiomatic: His enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Yangping Commandery with a fief of households as before.

sentences.zh: 車駕南伐，以沖兼左僕射，留守洛陽。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage marched south on campaign, Chong was made Concurrent Left Deputy Director and left to guard Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage marched south on campaign, Chong was made Concurrent Left Deputy Director and left to guard Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 車駕渡淮，別詔安南大將軍元英、平南將軍劉藻討漢中，召雍涇岐三州兵六千人擬戍南鄭，克城則遣。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage crossed the Huai, a separate edict ordered the General Who Pacifies the South, Yuan Ying, and the General Who Levels the South, Liu Zao, to attack Hanzhong, and summoned six thousand troops from Yong, Jing, and Qi Provinces to garrison Nanzheng — to be dispatched once the city was taken.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage crossed the Huai, a separate edict ordered the General Who Pacifies the South, Yuan Ying, and the General Who Levels the South, Liu Zao, to attack Hanzhong, and summoned six thousand troops from Yong, Jing, and Qi Provinces to garrison Nanzheng — to be dispatched once the city was taken.

sentences.zh: 沖表諫曰：「秦州險阨，地接羌夷，自西師出後，餉援連續，加氐胡叛逆，所在奔命，運糧擐甲，迄茲未已。

translations.literal: Chong submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "Qinzhou is rugged and defensible, its land bordering the Qiang and barbarians. Since the western army set out, supplies and reinforcements have flowed unceasingly. Added to this, the Di and Hu have rebelled; everywhere men run at the call to arms. Transporting grain and donning armor — to this day it has not ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Chong submitted a memorial of remonstrance: "Qinzhou is rugged and defensible, its land bordering the Qiang and barbarians. Since the western army set out, supplies and reinforcements have flowed unceasingly. Added to this, the Di and Hu have rebelled; everywhere men run at the call to arms. Transporting grain and donning armor — to this day it has not ceased.

sentences.zh: 今復豫差戍卒，懸擬山外，雖加優復，恐猶驚駭，脫終攻不克，徒動民情，連胡結夷，事或難測。

translations.literal: Now to pre-assign garrison troops, poised beyond the mountains — even with added exemptions and relief, I fear the people will still be alarmed. If the attack ultimately fails, we will have stirred the populace for nothing; linking Hu with barbarians, affairs may become hard to foresee.
translations.idiomatic: Now to pre-assign garrison troops, poised beyond the mountains — even with added exemptions and relief, I fear the people will still be alarmed. If the attack ultimately fails, we will have stirred the populace for nothing; linking Hu with barbarians, affairs may become hard to foresee.

sentences.zh: 輒依旨密下刺史，待軍克鄭城，然後差遣，如臣愚見，猶謂未足。

translations.literal: I have already followed the edict and secretly instructed the provincial governors: once the army takes Zheng City, then dispatch the troops. Yet in my humble view, even this still falls short.
translations.idiomatic: I have already followed the edict and secretly instructed the provincial governors: once the army takes Zheng City, then dispatch the troops. Yet in my humble view, even this still falls short.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 西道險阨，單徑千里，今欲深戍絕界之外，孤據羣賊之中，[15]敵攻不可卒援，食盡不可運糧。

translations.literal: The western route is rugged; a single path stretches a thousand li. Now you wish to garrison deeply beyond the farthest border, isolated among bandits,[15] where enemy attack cannot quickly be relieved and when food runs out grain cannot be transported.
translations.idiomatic: The western route is rugged; a single path stretches a thousand li. Now you wish to garrison deeply beyond the farthest border, isolated among bandits,[15] where enemy attack cannot quickly be relieved and when food runs out grain cannot be transported.

sentences.zh: 古人有言，『雖鞭之長，不及馬腹』，南鄭於國，實為馬腹也。

translations.literal: The ancients said, "Though the whip is long, it does not reach the horse's belly." Nanzheng to the state is truly the horse's belly.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, "Though the whip is long, it does not reach the horse's belly." Nanzheng to the state is truly the horse's belly.

sentences.zh: 且昔人攻伐，或城降而不取；

translations.literal: Moreover, when men of old campaigned, sometimes a city surrendered and they did not take it;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when men of old campaigned, sometimes a city surrendered and they did not take it;

sentences.zh: 仁君用師，或撫民而遺地。

translations.literal: a benevolent ruler used his army and sometimes comforted the people while leaving the land behind.
translations.idiomatic: a benevolent ruler used his army and sometimes comforted the people while leaving the land behind.

sentences.zh: 且王者之舉，情在拯民；

translations.literal: The purpose of a king's enterprise lies in saving the people;
translations.idiomatic: The purpose of a king's enterprise lies in saving the people;

sentences.zh: 夷寇所守，意在惜地。

translations.literal: what barbarian raiders hold to is cherishing land.
translations.idiomatic: what barbarian raiders hold to is cherishing land.

sentences.zh: 校之二義，德有淺深。

translations.literal: Weighing the two principles, virtue has its depths and shallows.
translations.idiomatic: Weighing the two principles, virtue has its depths and shallows.

sentences.zh: 惠聲已遠，何遽於一城哉？

translations.literal: Our benevolent name already reaches far — why rush after a single city?
translations.idiomatic: Our benevolent name already reaches far — why rush after a single city?

sentences.zh: 且魏境所掩，九州過八，民人所臣，十分而九。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Wei domain covers more than eight of the Nine Provinces; of the people who submit, nine parts in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Wei domain covers more than eight of the Nine Provinces; of the people who submit, nine parts in ten.

sentences.zh: 所未民者，惟漠北之與江外耳。

translations.literal: Those not yet subject are only the far north of the desert and the lands beyond the Yangzi.
