translations.idiomatic: Those not yet subject are only the far north of the desert and the lands beyond the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 羈之在近，豈急急於今日也？

translations.literal: To hold them loosely when they are near — must this be rushed today?
translations.idiomatic: To hold them loosely when they are near — must this be rushed today?

sentences.zh: 宜待大開疆宇，廣拔城聚，多積資糧，食足支敵，然後置邦樹將，為吞并之舉。

translations.literal: We ought to wait until the borders are greatly opened, cities and settlements widely taken, resources and grain abundantly stored, provisions sufficient to sustain the enemy — then establish provinces and appoint generals for a campaign of annexation.
translations.idiomatic: We ought to wait until the borders are greatly opened, cities and settlements widely taken, resources and grain abundantly stored, provisions sufficient to sustain the enemy — then establish provinces and appoint generals for a campaign of annexation.

sentences.zh: 今鍾離、壽陽，密邇未拔；

translations.literal: Now Zhongli and Shouyang lie close yet are not taken;
translations.idiomatic: Now Zhongli and Shouyang lie close yet are not taken;

sentences.zh: 赭城、新野，跬步弗降。

translations.literal: Zhe City and Xinye, a short step away, have not submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe City and Xinye, a short step away, have not submitted.

sentences.zh: [16]所克者舍之而不取，所降者撫之而旋戮。

translations.literal: [16]What we take we abandon rather than hold; those who submit we comfort and then execute.
translations.idiomatic: [16]What we take we abandon rather than hold; those who submit we comfort and then execute.

sentences.zh: 東道既未可以近力守，西蕃寧可以遠兵固？

translations.literal: If the eastern route cannot yet be held with nearby strength, can the western frontier truly be secured with distant troops?
translations.idiomatic: If the eastern route cannot yet be held with nearby strength, can the western frontier truly be secured with distant troops?

sentences.zh: 若果欲置者，臣恐終以資敵也。

translations.literal: If you truly intend to garrison it, I fear in the end it will only supply the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: If you truly intend to garrison it, I fear in the end it will only supply the enemy.

sentences.zh: 又今建都土中，地接寇壤，方須大收死士，平蕩江會。

translations.literal: Moreover, now that the capital is established in the Middle Land, our territory borders the enemy — we need urgently to gather resolute warriors and sweep clean the Yangzi junction.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, now that the capital is established in the Middle Land, our territory borders the enemy — we need urgently to gather resolute warriors and sweep clean the Yangzi junction.

sentences.zh: 輕遣單寡，棄令陷沒，恐後舉之日，眾以留守致懼，求其死効，未易可獲。

translations.literal: To lightly send a small, isolated force and abandon it to defeat — I fear that when the next campaign comes, the troops, fearful because of those left to garrison, will be hard to move to die in earnest service.
translations.idiomatic: To lightly send a small, isolated force and abandon it to defeat — I fear that when the next campaign comes, the troops, fearful because of those left to garrison, will be hard to move to die in earnest service.

sentences.zh: 推此而論，不戍為上。

translations.literal: Reasoning from this, not garrisoning is best.
translations.idiomatic: Reasoning from this, not garrisoning is best.

sentences.zh: 」高祖從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 車駕還都，引見沖等，謂之曰：「本所以多置官者，慮有令僕闇弱，百事稽壅，若明獨聰專，則權勢大併。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, the Emperor received Chong and the others and said to them: "The reason for establishing so many offices was the fear that some Director or Deputy Director might be dull and weak, and a hundred affairs become blocked. If one man alone were brilliant and shrewd, power would largely be combined.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, the Emperor received Chong and the others and said to them: "The reason for establishing so many offices was the fear that some Director or Deputy Director might be dull and weak, and a hundred affairs become blocked. If one man alone were brilliant and shrewd, power would largely be combined.

sentences.zh: [17]今朕雖不得為聰明，又不為劣闇，卿等不為大賢，亦不為大惡。

translations.literal: [17]Now I am neither able to be brilliantly wise, nor am I inferior and dull; you are neither greatly virtuous nor greatly wicked.
translations.idiomatic: [17]Now I am neither able to be brilliantly wise, nor am I inferior and dull; you are neither greatly virtuous nor greatly wicked.

sentences.zh: 且可一兩年許，少置官司。」

translations.literal: For a year or two, let us establish fewer offices."
translations.idiomatic: For a year or two, let us establish fewer offices."

sentences.zh: 高祖自鄴還京，汎舟洪池，乃從容謂沖曰：「朕欲從此通渠於洛，南伐之日，何容不從此入洛，從洛入河，從河入汴，從汴入清，以至於淮？

translations.literal: When the Emperor returned from Ye to the capital, he floated a boat on Hong Pool and then calmly said to Chong: "I wish to open a canal from here to Luoyang. On the day of the southern campaign, how could we fail to enter Luoyang from here, enter the river from Luoyang, enter the Bian from the river, enter the Qing from the Bian, until we reach the Huai?
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor returned from Ye to the capital, he floated a boat on Hong Pool and then calmly said to Chong: "I wish to open a canal from here to Luoyang. On the day of the southern campaign, how could we fail to enter Luoyang from here, enter the river from Luoyang, enter the Bian from the river, enter the Qing from the Bian, until we reach the Huai?

sentences.zh: 下船而戰，猶出戶而鬬，此乃軍國之大計。

translations.literal: To disembark and fight is like stepping out the door to battle — this is a great plan for army and state.
translations.idiomatic: To disembark and fight is like stepping out the door to battle — this is a great plan for army and state.

sentences.zh: 今溝渠若須二萬人以下、六十日有成者，宜以漸修之。

translations.literal: If a canal now requires fewer than twenty thousand men and can be completed in sixty days, it should be built gradually."
translations.idiomatic: If a canal now requires fewer than twenty thousand men and can be completed in sixty days, it should be built gradually."

sentences.zh: 」沖對曰：「若爾，便是士無遠涉之勞，戰有兼人之力。

translations.literal: Chong replied: "If so, then troops would be spared the toil of long marches, and in battle they would have the strength of more than one man."
translations.idiomatic: Chong replied: "If so, then troops would be spared the toil of long marches, and in battle they would have the strength of more than one man."

sentences.zh: 」遷尚書僕射，仍領少傅。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Deputy Director of the Secretariat, still retaining the Junior Tutorship.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Deputy Director of the Secretariat, still retaining the Junior Tutorship.

sentences.zh: 改封清淵縣開國侯，邑戶如前。

translations.literal: His enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Qingyuan County with a fief of households as before.
translations.idiomatic: His enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Qingyuan County with a fief of households as before.

sentences.zh: 乃太子恂廢，沖罷少傅。

translations.literal: When Crown Prince Xun was deposed, Chong was removed from the Junior Tutorship.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Xun was deposed, Chong was removed from the Junior Tutorship.

sentences.zh: 高祖引見公卿於清徽堂，高祖曰：「聖人之大寶，惟位與功，是以功成作樂，治定制禮。

translations.literal: The Emperor received the princes and officials at the Qingwei Hall and said: "The great treasure of the sage is position and achievement; therefore when achievement is complete one makes music, and when governance is settled one fixes ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor received the princes and officials at the Qingwei Hall and said: "The great treasure of the sage is position and achievement; therefore when achievement is complete one makes music, and when governance is settled one fixes ritual.

sentences.zh: 今徙極中天，創居嵩洛，雖大構未成，要自條紀略舉。

translations.literal: Now we have moved the capital to the center of Heaven, newly established our seat at Song and Luo. Though the great construction is not yet complete, the basic order must in general be set forth.
translations.idiomatic: Now we have moved the capital to the center of Heaven, newly established our seat at Song and Luo. Though the great construction is not yet complete, the basic order must in general be set forth.

sentences.zh: 但南有未賓之豎，兼兇蠻密邇，朕夙夜悵惋，良在於茲。

translations.literal: But in the south there are unsubmissive rebels, and fierce barbarians press close at hand. Day and night I grieve — truly the cause lies here.
translations.idiomatic: But in the south there are unsubmissive rebels, and fierce barbarians press close at hand. Day and night I grieve — truly the cause lies here.

sentences.zh: 取南之計決矣，朕行之謀必矣。

translations.literal: The plan to take the south is decided; my resolve to carry it out is firm.
translations.idiomatic: The plan to take the south is decided; my resolve to carry it out is firm.

sentences.zh: 若依近代也，則天子下帷深宮之內；

translations.literal: If one follows recent times, then the Son of Heaven sits behind lowered curtains deep within the palace;
translations.idiomatic: If one follows recent times, then the Son of Heaven sits behind lowered curtains deep within the palace;

sentences.zh: 準上古也，則有親行，祚延七百。

translations.literal: if one follows high antiquity, then there is personal campaigning, and the throne endured seven hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: if one follows high antiquity, then there is personal campaigning, and the throne endured seven hundred years.

sentences.zh: [18]魏晉不征，旋踵而殞，祚之修短，在德不在征。

translations.literal: [18]Wei and Jin did not campaign and swiftly perished; the length of a throne's endurance lies in virtue, not in campaigning.
translations.idiomatic: [18]Wei and Jin did not campaign and swiftly perished; the length of a throne's endurance lies in virtue, not in campaigning.

sentences.zh: 今但以行期未知早晚。

translations.literal: Now it is only that the date of the march is not yet known, early or late.
translations.idiomatic: Now it is only that the date of the march is not yet known, early or late.

sentences.zh: 知幾其神乎，朕既非神，焉能知也。

translations.literal: "To know the subtle before it appears — that is divine." I am not divine — how can I know?
translations.idiomatic: "To know the subtle before it appears — that is divine." I am not divine — how can I know?

sentences.zh: 而頃來陰陽卜術之士，咸勸朕今征必克。

translations.literal: Yet lately the masters of yin-yang and divination have all urged that if we campaign now we shall surely prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Yet lately the masters of yin-yang and divination have all urged that if we campaign now we shall surely prevail.

sentences.zh: 此既家國大事，宜共君臣各盡所見，不得以朕先言，便致依違，退有同異。

translations.literal: This is a great affair of state and dynasty; ruler and ministers alike must each give their full view. You may not, because I have spoken first, then hesitate in assent or dissent in retreat.
translations.idiomatic: This is a great affair of state and dynasty; ruler and ministers alike must each give their full view. You may not, because I have spoken first, then hesitate in assent or dissent in retreat.

sentences.zh: 」沖對曰：「夫征戰之法，先之人事，然後卜筮，今卜筮雖吉，猶恐人事未備。

translations.literal: Chong replied: "In the method of campaigning, human affairs come first, and only afterward divination. Now though divination is auspicious, I still fear human affairs are not yet ready.
translations.idiomatic: Chong replied: "In the method of campaigning, human affairs come first, and only afterward divination. Now though divination is auspicious, I still fear human affairs are not yet ready.

sentences.zh: 今年秋稔，有損常實，又京師始遷，眾業未定，加之征戰，以為未可。

translations.literal: This year's autumn harvest has fallen short of the usual yield. Moreover the capital has just been moved and the people's occupations are not yet settled. Added to a campaign — I consider it not yet feasible.
translations.idiomatic: This year's harvest falls short of the usual yield. The capital has just been moved and the people's livelihoods are not yet settled. To add a campaign on top of this — I do not think the time is right.

sentences.zh: 宜至來秋。

translations.literal: It should wait until next autumn.
translations.idiomatic: It should wait until next autumn.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「僕射之言，非為不合。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "What the Deputy Director says is not without reason.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "What the Deputy Director says is not without reason.

sentences.zh: 朕意之所慮，乃有社稷之憂。

translations.literal: What I myself worry about is a concern for the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: What I myself worry about is a concern for the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 然咫尺寇戎，無宜自安，理須如此。

translations.literal: Yet the enemy is close at hand; it is not fitting to rest at ease. By principle it must be so.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the enemy is close at hand; it is not fitting to rest at ease. By principle it must be so.

sentences.zh: 僕射言人事未從，亦不必如此。

translations.literal: What the Deputy Director says about human affairs not being ready need not be taken so far.
translations.idiomatic: What the Deputy Director says about human affairs not being ready need not be taken so far.

sentences.zh: 朕去十七年，擁二十萬眾，行不出畿甸，此人事之盛，而非天時。

translations.literal: Seventeen years ago I led two hundred thousand men and marched without leaving the capital region — that was the greatness of human affairs, not the season of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Seventeen years ago I led two hundred thousand men and marched without leaving the capital region — that was the greatness of human affairs, not the season of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 往年乘機，天時乃可，而闕人事，又致不捷。

translations.literal: In years past the season was favorable, yet because human affairs were lacking, victory was not achieved.
translations.idiomatic: In years past the season was favorable, yet because human affairs were lacking, victory was not achieved.

sentences.zh: 若待人事備，復非天時，若之何？

translations.literal: If we wait until human affairs are ready, it will no longer be the season of Heaven — what then?
translations.idiomatic: If we wait until human affairs are ready, it will no longer be the season of Heaven — what then?

sentences.zh: 如僕射之言，便終無征理。

translations.literal: By what the Deputy Director says, there would finally be no grounds for campaigning at all.
translations.idiomatic: By what the Deputy Director says, there would finally be no grounds for campaigning at all.

sentences.zh: 朕若秋行無克捷，三君子並付司寇。

translations.literal: If I campaign in autumn and there is no victory, the three of you will all be handed over to the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: If I campaign in autumn and there is no victory, the three of you will all be handed over to the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 不可不人盡其心。

translations.literal: Each of you must not fail to give your full heart."
translations.idiomatic: Each of you must not fail to give your full heart."

sentences.zh: 」罷議而出。

translations.literal: The deliberation ended and he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The deliberation ended and he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 後世宗為太子，高祖醼於清徽堂。

translations.literal: Later, when Shizong became Crown Prince, the Emperor held a banquet at the Qingwei Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Shizong became Crown Prince, the Emperor held a banquet at the Qingwei Hall.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「皇儲所以纂歷三才，光昭七祖，斯乃億兆咸悅，天人同泰，故延卿就此一醼，以暢忻情。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The Crown Prince exists to inherit the three powers and glorify the seven ancestors. This is what makes the myriad people rejoice and Heaven and man share felicity. Therefore I have invited you to this banquet to give full vent to our joy.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "The Crown Prince exists to inherit the three powers and glorify the seven ancestors. This is what makes the myriad people rejoice and Heaven and man share felicity. Therefore I have invited you to this banquet to give full vent to our joy.

sentences.zh: 」高祖又曰：「天地之道，一盈一虛，豈有常泰。

translations.literal: The Emperor also said: "The way of Heaven and Earth is one fullness and one emptiness — how could there be constant prosperity?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor also said: "The way of Heaven and Earth is one fullness and one emptiness — how could there be constant prosperity?

sentences.zh: 天道猶爾，況人事乎？

translations.literal: If the way of Heaven is so, how much more human affairs?
translations.idiomatic: If the way of Heaven is so, how much more human affairs?

sentences.zh: 故有升有黜，自古而然。

translations.literal: Therefore there is promotion and there is dismissal — it has been so since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore there is promotion and there is dismissal — it has been so since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 悼往欣今，良用深歎。

translations.literal: Mourning the past and rejoicing in the present — truly I sigh deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning the past and rejoicing in the present — truly I sigh deeply.

sentences.zh: 」沖對曰：「東暉承儲，蒼生咸幸。

translations.literal: Chong replied: "The Eastern Splendor inherits the succession; the common people are all blessed.
translations.idiomatic: Chong replied: "The Eastern Splendor inherits the succession; the common people are all blessed.

sentences.zh: 但臣前忝師傅，弗能弼諧，仰慚天日，慈造寬含，得預此醼，慶愧交深。

translations.literal: But I formerly served as tutor and failed to assist and harmonize. Looking up, I am ashamed before sun and sky; yet Your Majesty's gracious creation was broad and forgiving, allowing me to join this banquet — joy and shame mingle deeply.
translations.idiomatic: But I formerly served as tutor and failed to assist and harmonize. Looking up, I am ashamed before sun and sky; yet Your Majesty's gracious creation was broad and forgiving, allowing me to join this banquet — joy and shame mingle deeply.

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「朕尚弗能革其昏，師傅何勞愧謝也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I am still unable to reform his dullness — why should the tutor trouble himself with apologies?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "I am still unable to reform his dullness — why should the tutor trouble himself with apologies?"

sentences.zh: 後尚書疑元拔、穆泰罪事，沖奏曰：「前彭城鎮將元拔與穆泰同逆，養子降壽宜從拔罪。

translations.literal: Later, when the Ministry of Justice questioned the guilt of Yuan Ba and Mu Tai, Chong submitted a memorial: "Formerly the garrison commander of Pengcheng, Yuan Ba, joined Mu Tai in rebellion. The adopted son Jiang Shou should share Ba's guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Ministry of Justice questioned the guilt of Yuan Ba and Mu Tai, Chong submitted a memorial: "Formerly the garrison commander of Pengcheng, Yuan Ba, joined Mu Tai in rebellion. The adopted son Jiang Shou should share Ba's guilt.

sentences.zh: 而太尉、咸陽王禧等，以為律文養子而為罪，父及兄弟不知情者不坐。

translations.literal: But the Grand Commandant, Prince of Xianyang Xi, and others held that the law states: when an adopted son commits a crime, if the father and brothers did not know, they are not punished.
translations.idiomatic: But the Grand Commandant, Prince of Xianyang Xi, and others held that the law states: when an adopted son commits a crime, if the father and brothers did not know, they are not punished.

sentences.zh: 謹審律意，以養子於父非天性，於兄弟非同氣，敦薄既差，故刑典有降，是以養子雖為罪，而父兄不預。

translations.literal: Carefully examining the intent of the law: between an adopted son and the father there is no natural bond; between him and brothers there is no shared breath. Since the bond of affection is thinner, the penal code accordingly reduces punishment. Therefore though an adopted son commits a crime, father and brothers are not implicated.
translations.idiomatic: Carefully examining the intent of the law: between an adopted son and the father there is no natural bond; between him and brothers there is no shared breath. Since the bond of affection is thinner, the penal code accordingly reduces punishment. Therefore though an adopted son commits a crime, father and brothers are not implicated.

sentences.zh: 然父兄為罪，養子不知謀，易地均情，豈獨從戮乎？

translations.literal: Yet if the father and brothers commit a crime and the adopted son did not know the plot, by the same principle applied in reverse, should he alone be executed?
translations.idiomatic: Yet if the father and brothers commit a crime and the adopted son did not know the plot, by the same principle applied in reverse, should he alone be executed?

sentences.zh: 理固不然。

translations.literal: By principle this surely cannot be so.
translations.idiomatic: By principle this surely cannot be so.

sentences.zh: 臣以為：依據律文，不追戮於所生，則從坐於所養，[19]明矣。

translations.literal: I hold that according to the letter of the law, one is not pursued for punishment at the place of birth, but one is implicated at the place of adoption —[19] this is clear.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that according to the letter of the law, one is not pursued for punishment at the place of birth, but one is implicated at the place of adoption —[19] this is clear.

sentences.zh: 又律惟言父不從子，不稱子不從父，[20]當是優尊厲卑之義。

translations.literal: Moreover the law speaks only of the father not following the son, not of the son not following the father —[20] this must be the meaning of honoring the superior and restraining the inferior.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the law speaks only of the father not following the son, not of the son not following the father —[20] this must be the meaning of honoring the superior and restraining the inferior.

sentences.zh: 臣禧等以為：『律雖不正見，互文起制，於乞也舉父之罪，於養也見子坐，是為互起。

translations.literal: Minister Xi and others hold: "Though the law does not state it directly, cross-text establishes the rule: in the case of begging for adoption it cites the father's crime; in the case of adoption it shows the son's punishment — this is mutual establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Xi and others hold: "Though the law does not state it directly, cross-text establishes the rule: in the case of begging for adoption it cites the father's crime; in the case of adoption it shows the son's punishment — this is mutual establishment.

sentences.zh: 互起兩明，無罪必矣。

translations.literal: When both sides are mutually established, innocence is certain.
translations.idiomatic: When both sides are mutually established, innocence is certain.

sentences.zh: 若以嫡繼養與生同，則父子宜均，祇明不坐。

translations.literal: If one treats legitimate succession by adoption as the same as birth, then father and son should be equal — it need only state clearly that they are not punished.
translations.idiomatic: If one treats legitimate succession by adoption as the same as birth, then father and son should be equal — it need only state clearly that they are not punished.

sentences.zh: 且繼養之注云：若有別制，不同此律。

translations.literal: Moreover the commentary on succession by adoption says: if there is a separate statute, it differs from this law.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the commentary on succession by adoption says: if there is a separate statute, it differs from this law.

sentences.zh: 又令文云：諸有封爵，若無親子，及其身卒，雖有養繼，國除不襲。

translations.literal: Moreover the ordinance states: for all who hold enfeoffment, if there is no natural son, when they themselves die, though there is an adopted successor, the fief is abolished and not inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the ordinance states: for all who hold enfeoffment, if there is no natural son, when they themselves die, though there is an adopted successor, the fief is abolished and not inherited.

sentences.zh: 是為有福不及己，有罪便預坐。

translations.literal: This means that blessings do not reach oneself, but guilt is immediately shared in punishment.
translations.idiomatic: This means that blessings do not reach oneself, but guilt is immediately shared in punishment.

sentences.zh: 均事等情，律令之意，便相矛盾。

translations.literal: Equalizing affairs and equalizing sentiment, the intent of law and ordinance then contradict each other.
translations.idiomatic: Equalizing affairs and equalizing sentiment, the intent of law and ordinance then contradict each other.

sentences.zh: 伏度律旨，必不然也。

translations.literal: Reflecting on the intent of the law, it surely cannot be so.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on the intent of the law, it surely cannot be so.

sentences.zh: 』臣沖以為：指例條尋，罪在無疑，準令語情，頗亦同式。

translations.literal: "Minister Chong holds: citing precedents and searching the articles, guilt is beyond doubt; matching the ordinance to the sentiment of the language, it is also largely of the same form.
translations.idiomatic: "Minister Chong holds: citing precedents and searching the articles, guilt is beyond doubt; matching the ordinance to the sentiment of the language, it is also largely of the same form.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「僕射之議，據律明矣；

translations.literal: Edict: "The Deputy Director's reasoning, according to the law, is clear;
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "The Deputy Director's reasoning, according to the law, is clear;

sentences.zh: 太尉等論，於典矯也。

translations.literal: the Grand Commandant's discussion twists the canon."
translations.idiomatic: the Grand Commandant's discussion twists the canon."

sentences.zh: [21]養所以從戮者，緣其已免所生，故不得復甄於所養。

translations.literal: [21] The reason an adopted son is subject to execution is that, having already been exempted from punishment through his birth father, he cannot again be spared through his adoptive family.
translations.idiomatic: [21] An adopted son is executed because, once spared on account of his birth father, he cannot again be exempted through his adoptive family.

sentences.zh: 此獨何福，長處吞舟？

translations.literal: Why should this one alone enjoy such favor, forever exempt from the net that catches great offenders?
translations.idiomatic: Why should this one alone enjoy such favor, forever escaping the law that catches even great offenders?

sentences.zh: 于國所以不襲者，重列爵，特立制，因天之所絕，推而除之耳，豈復報對刑賞？

translations.literal: As for the reason a fief is not inherited, it is that noble rank is weighty and a separate statute was established; because Heaven has cut off the line, it is removed by decree — how could that be balanced against criminal reward and punishment?
translations.idiomatic: The reason a fief is not inherited is that noble rank is weighty and a separate statute was established: when Heaven cuts off a line, the state removes it by decree — that is hardly a matter of reciprocal criminal reward and punishment.

sentences.zh: 于斯則應死，可特原之。」

translations.literal: In this case he should die, but he may be specially pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: In this case he deserves death, but he may be specially pardoned."

sentences.zh: 沖機敏有巧思，北京明堂、圓丘、太廟，及洛都初基，安處郊兆，新起堂寢，皆資於沖。

translations.literal: Chong was quick-witted and full of ingenious ideas; the Bright Hall, the Circular Mound, and the Grand Ancestral Temple in the northern capital, and when Luoyang was first laid out — the placement of suburban altars and the construction of new halls and chambers — all relied on Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted and full of ingenious ideas, Chong designed the Bright Hall, Circular Mound, and Grand Ancestral Temple in the northern capital, and when Luoyang was first laid out he planned the suburban altars and new halls and chambers.

sentences.zh: 勤志強力，孜孜無怠，旦理文簿，兼營匠制，几案盈積，剞劂在手，終不勞厭也。

translations.literal: Diligent in will and strong in body, he toiled without slackening; by day he handled documents, and at the same time directed craftsmen — desks piled high, carving knife in hand, yet he never wearied of the labor.
translations.idiomatic: Diligent and tireless, he handled documents by day while directing craftsmen as well; with desks piled high and carving knife in hand, he never wearied of the work.

sentences.zh: 然顯貴門族，務益六姻，兄弟子姪，皆有爵官，一家歲祿，萬匹有餘，是其親者，雖復癡聾，無不超越官次。

translations.literal: Yet as a prominent noble clan, they sought to enrich their six kinds of kin; brothers, sons, and nephews all held titles and offices, and the family's annual stipend exceeded ten thousand bolts of silk. Among their relatives, even the dull and deaf all rose above their proper rank in office.
translations.idiomatic: Yet as a prominent noble house they enriched all six degrees of kin: brothers, sons, and nephews all held titles and offices, and the family's annual stipend exceeded ten thousand bolts of silk. Even dull or deaf relatives were promoted above their proper rank.

sentences.zh: 時論亦以此少之。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion also faulted him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion faulted him for this as well.

sentences.zh: 年纔四十，而鬢髮班白，姿貌豐美，未有衰狀。

translations.literal: Though only forty years old, his temples were already streaked with white; his bearing was full and handsome, with no sign of decline.
translations.idiomatic: Though only forty, his temples were already streaked with white; his bearing remained full and handsome, with no sign of decline.

sentences.zh: 李彪之入京也，孤微寡援，而自立不羣，以沖好士，傾心宗附。

translations.literal: When Li Biao came to the capital, he was isolated, humble, and short of support, yet stood apart from the crowd; because Chong favored men of talent, Biao devoted himself to him and joined his following.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Biao came to the capital he was isolated and without backing, yet stood apart from the crowd; because Chong favored talented men, Biao devoted himself to him and joined his circle.

sentences.zh: 沖亦重其器學，禮而納焉，每言之於高祖，公私共相援益。

translations.literal: Chong also valued his capacity and learning, received him with courtesy, spoke of him to Emperor Gaozu, and in public and private they mutually supported and benefited one another.
translations.idiomatic: Chong also valued his talent and learning, received him with courtesy, and commended him to Emperor Gaozu; in public and private they supported and benefited one another.

sentences.zh: 及彪為中尉、兼尚書，為高祖知待，便謂非復藉沖，而更相輕背，惟公坐斂袂而已，無復宗敬之意也。

translations.literal: When Biao became Commandant of Justice and concurrently Minister of the Masters of Writing, and won Emperor Gaozu's trust and favor, he decided he no longer needed Chong, and they turned to mutual disdain and estrangement; at court he merely drew in his sleeves — there was no longer any reverence for Chong as a patron.
translations.idiomatic: Once Biao became Commandant of Justice and concurrent Minister of the Masters of Writing and won the emperor's trust, he decided he no longer needed Chong; they grew mutually disdainful and estranged, and at court Biao merely drew in his sleeves, showing no further reverence for his former patron.

sentences.zh: 沖頗銜之。

translations.literal: Chong deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Chong deeply resented this.

sentences.zh: 後高祖南征，沖與吏部尚書、任城王澄並以彪倨傲無禮，遂禁止之。

translations.literal: Later, when Emperor Gaozu marched south, Chong and the Minister of the Civil Office, Prince of Rencheng Cheng, both charged Biao with arrogance and lack of courtesy, and had him placed under detention.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the emperor marched south, Chong and Minister of the Civil Office Prince Cheng of Rencheng charged Biao with arrogance and lack of courtesy and had him detained.

sentences.zh: 奏其罪狀，沖手自作，家人不知，辭甚激切，因以自劾。

translations.literal: He memorialized the charges in a document Chong wrote in his own hand, unknown to his household; the language was very sharp, and he thereby impeached himself as well.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted the charges in a memorial Chong wrote in his own hand, without his household's knowledge; the language was very sharp, and he thereby impeached himself as well.

sentences.zh: 高祖覽其表，歎悵者久之，既而曰：「道固可謂溢也，僕射亦為滿矣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu read the memorial, he sighed regretfully for a long time, then said: "The Way can indeed be said to overflow; the Vice Director is also full."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor read the memorial he sighed regretfully for a long time, then said, "The Way can indeed be said to overflow — and the Vice Director is also full."

sentences.zh: 」沖時震怒，[22]數數責彪前後愆悖，瞋目大呼，投折几案。

translations.literal: " Chong was then furious; [22] again and again he reproached Biao for his successive faults and insolence, glaring and shouting, hurling and breaking desks.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was then furious; [22] again and again he reproached Biao for his successive faults and insolence, glaring and shouting and hurling desks until they broke.

sentences.zh: 盡收御史，皆泥首面縛，詈辱肆口。

translations.literal: He seized all the censors, had them kneel with faces covered in mud and hands bound, and reviled them at will.
translations.idiomatic: He seized all the censors, had them kneel with mud-smeared faces and bound hands, and reviled them at will.

sentences.zh: 沖素性溫柔，而一旦暴恚，遂發病荒悸，言語亂錯，猶扼腕叫詈，稱李彪小人。

translations.literal: Chong was by nature gentle, yet in one sudden fit of rage he fell ill with delirium and palpitations; his speech became confused, yet he still clutched his wrist and shouted curses, calling Li Biao a petty man.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle by nature, Chong in one sudden fit of rage fell ill with delirium and palpitations; his speech became confused, yet he still clutched his wrist and shouted curses, calling Li Biao a petty man.

sentences.zh: 醫藥所不能療，或謂肝藏傷裂。

translations.literal: Medicine could not cure him; some said his liver had been ruptured.
translations.idiomatic: Medicine could not cure him; some said his liver had been ruptured.

sentences.zh: 旬有餘日而卒，時年四十九。

translations.literal: After a little more than ten days he died, at the age of forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: After a little more than ten days he died, at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 高祖為舉哀於懸瓠，發聲悲泣，不能自勝。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu held mourning for him at Xuanhuo, weeping aloud in grief beyond self-control.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held mourning for him at Xuanhuo, weeping aloud in grief beyond self-control.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「沖貞和資性，德義樹身，訓業自家，道素形國。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Chong's nature was upright and harmonious; he rooted himself in virtue and righteousness, trained in learning within his family, and his conduct shaped the state.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said, "Chong's nature was upright and harmonious; he rooted himself in virtue and righteousness, trained in learning within his family, and his conduct shaped the state.

sentences.zh: 太和之始，朕在弱齡，早委機密，實康時務。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Taihe reign, when I was still young, I early entrusted him with confidential affairs, and he truly brought order to the affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taihe reign, when I was still young, I early entrusted him with confidential affairs, and he truly brought order to the affairs of the age.

sentences.zh: 鴻漸瀍洛，朝選開清，升冠端右，惟允出納。

translations.literal: When the great enterprise advanced to the Chan and Luo rivers, court selection opened and became clear; he rose to the foremost place on the right and was truly fit to receive and deliver.
translations.idiomatic: When the great enterprise advanced to the Chan and Luo rivers, court selection opened and became clear; he rose to the foremost place on the right and was truly fit to receive and deliver imperial business.

sentences.zh: 忠肅柔明，足敷睿範，仁恭信惠，有結民心。

translations.literal: Loyal, reverent, gentle, and bright, he fully embodied the sage's model; benevolent, respectful, faithful, and gracious, he won the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal, reverent, gentle, and bright, he fully embodied the sage's model; benevolent, respectful, faithful, and gracious, he won the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 可謂國之賢也，朝之望也。

translations.literal: He may be called a worthy man of the state and the hope of the court.
translations.idiomatic: He may be called a worthy man of the state and the hope of the court.

sentences.zh: 方昇寵秩，以旌功舊，奄致喪逝，悲痛于懷。

translations.literal: Just as he was to rise in favor and rank to honor his long service, he suddenly passed away; grief fills my breast.
translations.idiomatic: Just as he was to rise in favor and rank to honor his long service, he suddenly passed away, and grief fills my breast.

sentences.zh: 既留勤應陟，兼良宿宜褒，可贈司空公，給東園祕器、朝服一具、衣一襲，贈錢三十萬、布五百匹、蠟二百斤。

translations.literal: Having long shown diligence deserving promotion, and being a fine elder worthy of praise, he may be posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of the Ministry of Works, granted the secret funerary objects of the Eastern Garden, one set of court robes, and one suit of clothing, with thirty thousand cash, five hundred bolts of cloth, and two hundred catties of wax given in gift.
translations.idiomatic: Having long shown diligence deserving promotion, and being a fine elder worthy of praise, he is posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of the Ministry of Works, granted the secret funerary objects of the Eastern Garden, one set of court robes, and one suit of clothing, with thirty thousand cash, five hundred bolts of cloth, and two hundred catties of wax given in gift.

sentences.zh: 」有司奏諡曰文穆。

translations.literal: " The responsible offices memorialized that his posthumous title should be Wenmu.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible offices memorialized that his posthumous title should be Wenmu.

sentences.zh: 葬於覆舟山，近杜預冢，高祖之意也。

translations.literal: He was buried on Mount Fuzhou, near the tomb of Du Yu — at Emperor Gaozu's wish.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried on Mount Fuzhou, near the tomb of Du Yu — at the emperor's wish.

sentences.zh: 後車駕自鄴還洛，路經沖墓，左右以聞，高祖臥疾望墳，掩泣久之。

sentences.zh: 按大將軍第一品，班在三公上

translations.literal: Examining: Grand General is first rank, ranking above the Three Dukes
translations.idiomatic: Grand General is first rank, ranking above the Three Dukes

sentences.zh: 〈見卷一一三官氏志〉

translations.literal: (see Monograph on Offices and Clans, juan 113)
translations.idiomatic: (see Monograph on Offices and Clans, juan 113)

sentences.zh: ，與所除之散騎常侍、左光祿大夫、都官尚書等官品不相當。

translations.literal: , which does not match the ranks of the offices to which he was appointed — Regular Attendant, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: , which does not match the ranks of the offices to which he was appointed — Regular Attendant, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 且李郁死後贈驃騎大將軍，豈有生前已為大將軍之理。

translations.literal: Moreover, after Li Yu's death he was posthumously enfeoffed as General of Agile Cavalry — how could he already have been Grand General in life?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, after Li Yu's death he was posthumously enfeoffed as General of Agile Cavalry — how could he already have been Grand General in life?

sentences.zh: 這裏「大將軍」上當脫「衞」字。

translations.literal: Here the character "Guard" must be missing before "Grand General."
translations.idiomatic: Here the character "Guard" must be missing before "Grand General."

sentences.zh: 比後月十間 冊府卷五四一

translations.literal: "Within the next ten months or so" — Cefu juan 541
translations.idiomatic: "Within the next ten months or so": Cefu, juan 541

sentences.zh: 〈六四八五頁〉
「月十」作「十月」，疑是。

translations.literal: writes "month ten" as "tenth month"; this is probably correct.
translations.idiomatic: reads "month ten" as "tenth month"; this is probably correct.

sentences.zh: 前南安王楨進曰 諸本無「前」字，北史卷三三李沖傳、冊府卷一三

translations.literal: "Former Prince of Nan'an Zhen stepped forward and said" — all editions lack the character "former"; Beishi juan 33, biography of Li Chong, and Cefu juan 13
translations.idiomatic: "Former Prince of Nan'an Zhen stepped forward and said": all editions lack the character "former"; Beishi, juan 33, biography of Li Chong, and Cefu, juan 13

sentences.zh: 〈一四八頁〉
有。

translations.literal: have it.
translations.idiomatic: have it.

sentences.zh: 按卷一九下南安王楨傳，楨先以聚斂「削除官爵，禁錮終身」，後以議定遷都，復封。

translations.literal: Examining juan 19, Part 2, biography of Prince of Nan'an Zhen: Zhen was first, for extortion, "stripped of office and rank and imprisoned for life," then restored to his fief for his part in deciding the transfer of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: According to juan 19, Part 2, biography of Prince Zhen of Nan'an: Zhen was first, for extortion, "stripped of office and rank and imprisoned for life," then restored to his fief for his part in deciding the transfer of the capital.

sentences.zh: 這時王爵未復，故稱「前」。

translations.literal: At this time his princely title had not yet been restored, hence he is called "former."
translations.idiomatic: At this time his princely title had not yet been restored, hence he is called "former."

sentences.zh: 冊府採魏書而與北史同，知這裏脫「前」字，今據補。

translations.literal: Cefu drew on Wei Shu and agrees with Beishi; knowing that "former" is missing here, it is now supplied according to this evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Cefu drew on Wei Shu and agrees with Beishi; knowing that "former" is missing here, it is now supplied accordingly.

sentences.zh: 非常之人乃能建非常之事 諸本「乃能」下脫「建」字，今據冊府卷一三

translations.literal: "Only extraordinary men can accomplish extraordinary deeds" — all editions omit the character "establish" after "can"; now according to Cefu juan 13
translations.idiomatic: "Only extraordinary men can accomplish extraordinary deeds": all editions omit the character "establish" after "can"; restored according to Cefu, juan 13

sentences.zh: 〈一四八頁〉
補。

translations.literal: Supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Supplied.

sentences.zh: 孤據羣賊之中 諸本「中」作「口」，冊府卷五三０

translations.literal: "Alone holding out among a host of bandits" — all editions write "among" as "mouth"; Cefu juan 530
translations.idiomatic: "Alone holding out among a host of bandits": all editions read "among" as "mouth"; Cefu, juan 530

sentences.zh: 〈六三二七頁〉
、通鑑卷一四０

translations.literal: and Zizhi tongjian juan 140
translations.idiomatic: and Zizhi tongjian, juan 140

sentences.zh: 〈四三八三頁〉
並作「中」。

translations.literal: all write "among."
translations.idiomatic: all have "among."

sentences.zh: 按「中」和上「深戍絕界之外」相對，「口」字訛，今據改。

translations.literal: Examining: "among" corresponds above to "deep garrisons beyond the frontier boundary"; the character "mouth" is corrupt; corrected now according to this evidence.
translations.idiomatic: "Among" corresponds above to "deep garrisons beyond the frontier boundary"; the character "mouth" is corrupt; the text is emended accordingly.

sentences.zh: 赭城新野跬步弗降 諸本「赭」作「諸」，通鑑卷一四０

translations.literal: "Zhecheng and Xinye did not submit at every step" — all editions write "Zhe" as "Zhu"; Zizhi tongjian juan 140
translations.idiomatic: "Zhecheng and Xinye did not submit at every step": all editions read "Zhe" as "Zhu"; Zizhi tongjian, juan 140

sentences.zh: 〈四三八三頁〉
作「赭」，考異不言有異文。

translations.literal: writes "Zhe"; Kaoyi does not note variant readings.
translations.idiomatic: has "Zhe"; Kaoyi does not note variant readings.

sentences.zh: 按卷一０六中地形志中南青州東莞郡有諸縣，也即漢琅邪郡的諸縣，故城在今山東諸城縣西南。

translations.literal: Examining juan 106, Part 2, Treatise on Geography, Southern Qing Province, Dongguan Commandery has Zhu County — that is, the Zhu County of Han's Langye Commandery; its old city is southwest of present-day Zhucheng County in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: According to juan 106, Part 2, Treatise on Geography, Southern Qing Province, Dongguan Commandery has Zhu County — that is, the Zhu County of Han's Langye Commandery; its old city is southwest of present-day Zhucheng County in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 其地自皇興三年

translations.literal: That region, from the third year of Huangxing
translations.idiomatic: That region, from the third year of Huangxing

sentences.zh: 〈四六九〉
慕容白曜取青州後，久屬北魏，不得云「跬步弗降」。

translations.literal: after Murong Baiyao took Qing Province, long belonged to Northern Wei — one cannot say "did not submit at every step."
translations.idiomatic: after Murong Baiyao took Qing Province, long belonged to Northern Wei — one cannot say "did not submit at every step."

sentences.zh: 「赭城」即赭陽

translations.literal: "Zhecheng" is Zheyang
translations.idiomatic: "Zhecheng" is Zheyang

sentences.zh: 〈見通鑑胡注〉

translations.literal: (see Hu annotation to Zizhi tongjian)
translations.idiomatic: (see Hu annotation to Zizhi tongjian)

sentences.zh: ，和新野都是南齊邊界要地，太和二十一年

translations.literal: , and Xinye were both key places on the Southern Qi frontier; in the twenty-first year of Taihe
translations.idiomatic: , and Xinye were both key places on the Southern Qi frontier; in the twenty-first year of Taihe

sentences.zh: 〈四九七〉
元宏親自統軍南下，赭陽、新野始被攻佔

translations.literal: Yuan Hong personally commanded the army south; only then were Zheyang and Xinye captured
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hong personally commanded the army south; only then were Zheyang and Xinye captured

sentences.zh: 〈見卷七下高祖紀下〉

translations.literal: (see Basic Annals of Emperor Gaozu, Part 2, juan 7)
translations.idiomatic: (see Basic Annals of Emperor Gaozu, Part 2, juan 7)

sentences.zh: 這裏「諸」字顯為「赭」字形訛，今據通鑑改。

translations.literal: Here the character "Zhu" is clearly a graphic corruption of "Zhe"; corrected now according to Zizhi tongjian.
translations.idiomatic: Here the character "Zhu" is clearly a graphic corruption of "Zhe"; the text is emended according to Zizhi tongjian.

sentences.zh: 若明獨聰專則權勢大併 冊府卷四六

translations.literal: "If clear, alone, perceptive, and exclusive, then power and authority greatly merge" — Cefu juan 46
translations.idiomatic: "If clear, alone, perceptive, and exclusive, then power and authority greatly merge": Cefu, juan 46

sentences.zh: 〈五二二頁〉
此句作「若明，則聽斷獨專；

translations.literal: This sentence reads: "If clear, then judgment and decision are exclusively one's own;
translations.idiomatic: This sentence reads, "If clear, then judgment and decision are exclusively one's own;

sentences.zh: 聰，則權勢大併」，語意較明白，疑傳本訛脫。

translations.literal: if perceptive, then power and authority greatly merge" — the sense is clearer; the transmitted text is suspected of corruption and omission.
translations.idiomatic: if perceptive, then power and authority greatly merge" — the sense is clearer; the transmitted text is suspected of corruption and omission.

sentences.zh: 準上古也則有親行祚延七百 冊府卷五七

translations.literal: "Matching antiquity, then there is personal campaigning and the throne endures seven hundred years" — Cefu juan 57
translations.idiomatic: "Matching antiquity, then there is personal campaigning and the throne endures seven hundred years": Cefu, juan 57

sentences.zh: 〈六三四頁〉
「親行」上有「周武」二字。

translations.literal: Above "personal campaigning" are the two characters "Zhou Wu."
translations.idiomatic: Above "personal campaigning" are the two characters "Zhou Wu."

sentences.zh: 按「周武親行，祚延七百」與下「魏晉不征，旋踵而殞」相對。

translations.literal: Examining: "Zhou Wu campaigned in person, and the throne endured seven hundred years" corresponds below to "Wei and Jin did not campaign, and perished in the turning of a heel."
translations.idiomatic: "Zhou Wu campaigned in person, and the throne endured seven hundred years" corresponds below to "Wei and Jin did not campaign, and perished in the turning of a heel."

sentences.zh: 「則有」下當有脫文，冊府殘存「周武」二字，但所脫不止此，「則有」下當有與上句「天子下帷深宮之內」作對的幾個字，然後接「周武親征」云云。

translations.literal: Below "then there is" there must be missing text; Cefu preserves the two characters "Zhou Wu," but what is missing is not limited to this — below "then there is" there should be several characters parallel to the line above, "the Son of Heaven within the deep palace with curtains lowered," and then "Zhou Wu campaigned in person" and so on.
translations.idiomatic: Below "then there is" there must be missing text; Cefu preserves the two characters "Zhou Wu," but what is missing is not limited to this — below "then there is" there should be several characters parallel to the line above, "the Son of Heaven within the deep palace with curtains lowered," and then "Zhou Wu campaigned in person" and so on.

sentences.zh: 不追戮於所生則從坐於所養 諸本「追」上無「不」字。

translations.literal: "Not pursuing execution through the birth father, then implicated through the adoptive family" — all editions lack the character "not" before "pursue."
translations.idiomatic: "Not pursuing execution through the birth father, then implicated through the adoptive family": all editions lack the character "not" before "pursue."

sentences.zh: 冊府卷六一五

translations.literal: Cefu juan 615
translations.idiomatic: Cefu, juan 615

sentences.zh: 〈七三九一頁〉
有。

translations.literal: has it.
translations.idiomatic: has it.

sentences.zh: 按李沖意謂據律文，養子不因生父犯罪而連坐，那麼養父犯罪就該連坐。

translations.literal: Examining: Li Chong's meaning is that according to the law text, an adopted son is not implicated when his birth father commits a crime; therefore when the adoptive father commits a crime he should be implicated.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong's meaning is that according to the law text, an adopted son is not implicated when his birth father commits a crime; therefore when the adoptive father commits a crime he should be implicated.

sentences.zh: 無「不」字不可通，今據補。

translations.literal: Without the character "not" the text is untenable; supplied now according to this evidence.
translations.idiomatic: Without the character "not" the text is untenable; it is now supplied accordingly.

sentences.zh: 不稱子不從父 百衲本此句作「稱子不不從父」，顯誤，北本、汲本、殿本作「稱子不從父」，南本、局本如上摘句。

translations.literal: "Does not say that the son does not follow the father" — the Baiwan edition of this sentence reads "says son not-not follow father," which is clearly wrong; the Northern, Ji, and Palace editions read "says son not follow father"; the Southern and Bureau editions read as in the excerpt above.
translations.idiomatic: "Does not say that the son does not follow the father": the Baiwan edition of this sentence reads "says son not-not follow father," which is clearly wrong; the Northern, Ji, and Palace editions read "says son not follow father"; the Southern and Bureau editions read as in the excerpt above.

sentences.zh: 冊府

translations.literal: Cefu
translations.idiomatic: Cefu

sentences.zh: 〈同上卷頁〉

translations.literal: (same juan and page)
translations.idiomatic: (same juan and page)

sentences.zh: 作「不言子不從父」。

translations.literal: writes "does not say son not follow father."
translations.idiomatic: reads "does not say son not follow father."

sentences.zh: 按百衲本「稱」上「不」字誤移在「子」字下，致不成語，北、汲、殿三本刪一「不」字，上下語意不貫，冊府「稱」字作「言」，但上同有「不」字，知南本、局本是，今從之。

translations.literal: Examining: in the Baiwan edition the character "not" above "says" was wrongly moved below "son," making the phrase unintelligible; the Northern, Ji, and Palace editions delete one "not," but the sense above and below does not cohere; in Cefu the character "says" is written "speak," but above it likewise has "not," so the Southern and Bureau editions are correct; the text follows them.
translations.idiomatic: In the Baiwan edition the character "not" above "says" was wrongly moved below "son," making the phrase unintelligible; the Northern, Ji, and Palace editions delete one "not," but the sense above and below does not cohere; in Cefu the character "says" is written "speak," but above it likewise has "not," so the Southern and Bureau editions are correct; the text follows them.

sentences.zh: 於典矯也 諸本「典」訛「曲」，不可通，今據冊府

translations.literal: "Distorts the canon" — all editions corrupt "canon" as "bent"; the text is untenable; now according to Cefu
translations.idiomatic: "Distorts the canon": all editions corrupt "canon" as "bent"; the text is untenable; restored according to Cefu

sentences.zh: 〈同上卷頁〉

translations.literal: (same juan and page)
translations.idiomatic: (same juan and page)

sentences.zh: 改。

translations.literal: Corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Corrected.

sentences.zh: 沖時震怒 諸本「怒」作「恐」，北史卷一００自序、冊府卷四七八

translations.literal: "Chong was then furious" — all editions write "furious" as "fearful"; Beishi juan 100, author's preface, and Cefu juan 478
translations.idiomatic: "Chong was then furious": all editions read "furious" as "fearful"; Beishi, juan 100, author's preface, and Cefu, juan 478

sentences.zh: 〈五七一０頁〉
作「怒」。

translations.literal: write "furious."
translations.idiomatic: have "furious."

sentences.zh: 按下文極言李沖暴怒之狀，且李彪與沖權勢不敵，沖何故震恐？

translations.literal: Examining: the text below strongly describes Li Chong's violent rage, and Li Biao's power did not match Chong's — why should Chong have been stricken with fear?
translations.idiomatic: The text below strongly describes Li Chong's violent rage, and Li Biao's power did not match Chong's — why should Chong have been stricken with fear?

sentences.zh: 「恐」乃「怒」之形訛，今據改。

translations.literal: "Fearful" is a graphic corruption of "furious"; corrected now according to this evidence.
translations.idiomatic: "Fearful" is a graphic corruption of "furious"; the text is emended accordingly.
